sentences.zh: 李穀，字惟珍，潁州汝陰人。

translations.literal: Li Gu, courtesy name Weizhen, was a native of Ruyin in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu, whose courtesy name was Weizhen, came from Ruyin in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，容貌魁偉。

translations.literal: He was eight chi tall, with a towering and imposing appearance.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi in height, with a tall and imposing bearing.

sentences.zh: 少勇力善射，以任俠為事，頗為鄉人所困，發憤從學，所覽如宿習。

translations.literal: In youth he was brave and strong and skilled at archery; he made chivalrous deeds his occupation and was much troubled by fellow townsmen. He resolved in anger to pursue learning, and whatever he read seemed like long-familiar study.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was bold and powerful and excelled at archery. He lived as a knight-errant and was often at odds with his neighbors, until in frustration he turned to study; everything he read seemed to come back to him as if he had known it all along.

sentences.zh: 年二十七，舉進士，連辟華、泰二州從事。

translations.literal: At age twenty-seven he passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly summoned as an aide in Hua and Tai prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-seven he passed the jinshi examination and was successively appointed aide in Hua and Tai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 開運二年秋，出為磁州刺史、北面水陸轉運使。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Kaiyun, he went out as prefect of Cizhou and commissioner for northern land-and-water transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Kaiyun 2, he was sent out as prefect of Cizhou and commissioner for northern land-and-water transport.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，少帝蒙塵而北，舊臣無敢候謁者，穀獨拜迎於路，君臣相對泣下。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, the Young Emperor suffered exile to the north. None of the former ministers dared to wait upon and greet him; Gu alone bowed and received him on the road, lord and minister facing each other in tears.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Bian, the deposed emperor was borne north in disgrace. None of his former ministers dared to meet him on the road—only Gu bowed to receive him, and ruler and subject wept face to face.

sentences.zh: 穀曰：“臣無狀，負陛下。”

translations.literal: Gu said, "Your servant is worthless and has failed Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "I am unworthy and have failed Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 因傾囊以獻。

translations.literal: Thereupon he emptied his purse and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He then emptied his purse and offered everything he had.

sentences.zh: 會契丹主發使至州，穀禽斬之，密送款於漢祖，潛遣河朔酋豪梁暉入據安陽，契丹主患之，即議北旋。

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler sent envoys to the prefecture, Gu seized and executed them, secretly sent allegiance to the Han founder, and covertly dispatched the Hebei chieftain Liang Hui to enter and hold Anyang. The Khitan ruler was troubled by this and at once deliberated on returning north.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan emperor sent envoys to his prefecture, Gu seized and executed them, secretly pledged loyalty to the founder of Later Han, and quietly sent the Hebei magnate Liang Hui to seize Anyang. Troubled by this, the Khitan ruler soon decided to withdraw north.

sentences.zh: 會有告契丹以城中虛弱者，契丹還攻安陽，陷其城，穀自郡候契丹，遂見獲。

translations.literal: Someone reported to the Khitan that the city was weakly defended. The Khitan turned back to attack Anyang, took the city, and Gu went from the prefecture to wait upon the Khitan and was thereupon captured.
translations.idiomatic: Someone informed the Khitan that the city was poorly defended. They returned to attack Anyang, captured it, and when Gu came from the prefecture to present himself to the Khitan, he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 契丹主先設刑具，謂之曰：“爾何背我歸太原？”

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler first set out instruments of punishment and said to him, "Why did you turn against me and go over to Taiyuan?"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler first had torture implements set out and said to him, "Why did you betray me and go over to Taiyuan?"

sentences.zh: 穀曰：“無之。”

translations.literal: Gu said, "There was no such thing."
translations.idiomatic: Gu replied, "Nothing of the kind."

sentences.zh: 契丹主因引手車中，似取所獲文字，而穀知其詐，因請曰：“如實有此事，乞顯示之。”

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler then reached into the carriage as if to take out captured documents, but Gu knew it was a deception and therefore requested, "If this truly happened, I beg that it be shown."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler reached into his carriage as if to produce captured documents, but Gu knew it was a bluff and said, "If this really happened, please show me the evidence."

sentences.zh: 契丹國制，人未伏者不即置死。

translations.literal: By Khitan state law, one who had not submitted was not immediately put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Under Khitan law, a man who had not yet submitted was not executed at once.

sentences.zh: 自後凡詰穀者六次，穀詞不屈。

translations.literal: Afterward, whenever Gu was interrogated—six times in all—his words did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Gu was questioned six times in all, and each time his answers never wavered.

sentences.zh: 契丹主病，且曰：“我南行時，人云爾謂我必不得北還，爾何術知之？

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler fell ill and also said, "When I marched south, people said you declared that I would certainly not return north. By what art did you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan ruler fell ill, he also said, "When I marched south, people said you had predicted I would never return north. What magic told you that?"

sentences.zh: 今我疾甚，如能救我，則致爾富貴。”

translations.literal: Now my illness is severe. If you can save me, I will bring you wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: Now I am gravely ill. If you can cure me, I will make you rich and honored.

sentences.zh: 穀曰：“實無術，蓋為人所陷耳。”

translations.literal: Gu said, "There truly is no art; I was simply framed by others."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "I have no such power at all—I was merely set up by others."

sentences.zh: 穀氣色不撓，卒寬之。

translations.literal: Gu's bearing did not falter, and in the end he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Gu's composure never broke, and in the end he was spared.

sentences.zh: 俄而德光道殂，永康繼立，署穀給事中。

translations.literal: Before long Deguang died on the road; Yongkang succeeded to the throne and appointed Gu as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Deguang died on the march; Empress Dowager Yingtian took power and appointed Gu Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 時契丹將麻答守真定，而李崧、和凝與家屬皆在城中。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan general Mada held Zhending, while Li Song, He Ning, and their families were all in the city.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Khitan general Mada held Zhending, and Li Song, He Ning, and their families were all inside the city.

sentences.zh: 會李筠、何福進率兵逐麻答，推護聖指揮使白再榮權知留後。

translations.literal: When Li Yun and He Fujin led troops to drive out Mada, they promoted the Protecting-the-Sage director Bai Zairong to act as provisional military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun and He Fujin then led troops to expel Mada and installed the Protecting-the-Sage director Bai Zairong as acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 再榮利崧等家財，令甲士圍其居以求賂，既得之，復欲殺崧等滅口。

translations.literal: Zairong coveted the family wealth of Song and the others, ordered armored soldiers to surround their residences to extort bribes, and after obtaining them still wished to kill Song and the others to silence them.
translations.idiomatic: Zairong coveted the wealth of Song and his colleagues, sent soldiers to surround their homes to extort bribes, and once he had the money still planned to kill them to silence witnesses.

sentences.zh: 穀遽見再榮謂之曰：“今國亡主辱，公輩握勁兵，不能死節，雖逐一契丹將，城中戰死者數千人，非獨公之力也。

translations.literal: Gu hastened to see Zairong and said to him, "Now the state is perished and the ruler disgraced. You gentlemen hold strong troops yet could not die for principle. Though you drove out one Khitan general, several thousand died fighting in the city—not by your strength alone."
translations.idiomatic: Gu hurried to see Zairong and said, "The state is lost and the sovereign humiliated. You hold strong armies yet failed to die for your lord. Though you drove out one Khitan general, thousands died in the fighting—not by your power alone."

sentences.zh: 一朝殺宰相，即日中原有主，責公以專殺，其將何辭以對？”

translations.literal: If in a single morning you kill a chief minister, that very day the Central Plains will have a ruler who will charge you with unauthorized killing—what words will you have to answer?"
translations.idiomatic: Kill a chief minister in one morning, and that very day the Central Plains will have a master who will charge you with murder on your own authority—what defense will you offer?

sentences.zh: 再榮甚懼，崧等獲免。

translations.literal: Zairong was greatly afraid, and Song and the others were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Zairong was terrified, and Song and the others were spared.

sentences.zh: 漢初，入拜左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, he entered court and was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Han was founded, he entered court and was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 舊制，罷外郡歸本官，至是進秩，獎之也。

translations.literal: By old regulation, on leaving an outer prefecture one returned to one's original office; on this occasion he was advanced in rank, a reward.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, leaving a provincial post meant reverting to one's former rank; this time he was promoted instead, as a reward.

sentences.zh: 俄權判開封府。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made acting administrator of the Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed acting administrator of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 時京畿多盜，中牟尤甚，穀誘邑人發其巢穴。

translations.literal: At that time there were many bandits in the capital region, especially at Zhongmou. Gu induced local people to expose their dens.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rife around the capital, worst of all at Zhongmou. Gu persuaded locals to reveal their hideouts.

sentences.zh: 有劉德輿者，梁時屢攝畿佐，居中牟，素有幹材，穀即署攝本邑主簿。

translations.literal: There was one Liu Deyu who had repeatedly served as acting aide in the capital region under Liang, resided at Zhongmou, and was known for administrative talent. Gu at once appointed him acting chief clerk of that county.
translations.idiomatic: One Liu Deyu had often served in capital posts under Later Liang and lived at Zhongmou; he was known as capable. Gu immediately appointed him acting chief clerk of the county.

sentences.zh: 浹旬，穀請侍衛兵數千佐德輿，悉禽賊黨，其魁一即縣佐史，一御史臺吏。

translations.literal: Within ten days Gu requested several thousand palace guards to assist Deyu; they captured the whole band of thieves. Of the ringleaders, one was a county aide-clerk and one a censorate clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Gu obtained several thousand palace guards to assist Deyu. The entire gang was captured; one leader was a county aide, the other a censorate clerk.

sentences.zh: 搜其家，得金玉財貨甚眾，自是行者無患。

translations.literal: Searching their homes yielded a great quantity of gold, jade, and valuables. From then on travelers had no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Searches of their homes turned up vast hoards of gold, jade, and goods. After that, travelers went unharmed.

sentences.zh: 俄遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 周祖西征，為西南面行營水陸轉運使。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder marched west, Gu served as commissioner for land-and-water transport of the southwestern campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder of Later Zhou marched west, Gu served as commissioner for land-and-water transport of the southwestern campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 關右平，改陳州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Guan region was pacified, he was changed to prefect of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: After the Guan region was pacified, he was made prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 會有內難，急召赴闕。

translations.literal: When internal strife arose, he was urgently summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When civil strife broke out, he was urgently summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 周祖兵入汴，命權判三司。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder's army entered Bian, he was ordered to act as administrator of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder's army entered Bian, Gu was ordered to act as administrator of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，加戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was given the additional title of Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangshun era he was made Vice Minister of Revenue as well.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜中書侍郎、平章事，仍判三司。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, while still administering the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, while continuing to administer the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 初，漢乾祐中，周祖討河中，穀掌轉運，時周祖已有人望，屬漢政紊亂，潛貯異志，屢以諷穀，穀但對以人臣當盡節奉上而已。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Qianyou era of Han, when the Zhou founder campaigned against Hezhong, Gu managed transport. At that time the Zhou founder already enjoyed popular regard; as Han government was in disorder he secretly harbored a different intent and repeatedly hinted at it to Gu, but Gu only replied that as a minister one should exhaust loyalty in serving the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Qianyou era of Later Han, when the Zhou founder campaigned against Hezhong, Gu managed supplies. The founder already enjoyed wide esteem; with Han politics in chaos he secretly nursed larger ambitions and often sounded Gu out, but Gu would only say that a minister must serve his sovereign with full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 故開國之初，倚以為相。

translations.literal: Therefore at the founding of the state he relied on him as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: That is why, at the founding of the dynasty, he relied on Gu as his chief minister.

sentences.zh: 是歲，淮陽吏民數千詣闕請立生祠，許之，穀懇讓得止。

translations.literal: That year several thousand officials and commoners of Huaiyang came to court requesting a living shrine; permission was granted, but Gu earnestly declined and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: That year several thousand people from Huaiyang petitioned the court for a living shrine in his honor. Though approval was granted, Gu firmly declined and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 先是，禁牛革法甚峻，犯者抵死。

translations.literal: Previously the law forbidding cattle hide was very severe; violators were punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the ban on cattle hide had been extremely harsh—violators faced death.

sentences.zh: 穀乃校每歲用革之數，凡田十頃歲出一革，餘聽民私用。

translations.literal: Gu then calculated the annual amount of hide used: for every ten qing of fields one hide per year, and the remainder was left to private use by the people.
translations.idiomatic: Gu then calculated annual hide requirements: one hide per year for every ten qing of farmland, with the rest free for private use.

sentences.zh: 又奏罷屯田務，以民隸州縣課役，盡除宿弊。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to abolish the garrison-field office, assigning the people to prefecture and county corvée duties, and completely removed longstanding abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to abolish the garrison-field office, assigning the people to normal prefectural and county labor duties, and swept away long-standing abuses.

sentences.zh: 穀父祖本居河南洛陽，經巢之亂，園廬蕩盡，穀生於外。

translations.literal: Gu's father and grandfather had originally lived in Luoyang, Henan. After the disorders of Huang Chao, gardens and houses were utterly swept away, and Gu was born abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Gu's forebears had lived in Luoyang, Henan. Huang Chao's rebellion destroyed their estates entirely, and Gu was born away from home.

sentences.zh: 既貴，訪得舊地，建蘭若，又立垣屋，凡族人之不可仕者分田居之。

translations.literal: Once he had risen high, he sought out the old site, built a Buddhist monastery, and also erected walled dwellings; all kinsmen unfit for office were given fields and housed there.
translations.idiomatic: After he rose to high rank, he found the old family lands, built a monastery, and erected walled dwellings, giving fields and homes to kinsmen who could not serve in office.

sentences.zh: 詔改清風鄉高陽里為賢相鄉勳德里。

translations.literal: An edict changed Qingfeng township's Gaoyang lane to Xianxiang township's Xunde lane.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed Qingfeng township's Gaoyang lane to Worthy Minister township, Merit lane.

sentences.zh: 二年，晨起仆階下，傷右臂，在告，旬中三上表辭相位，周祖不允，免朝參，視事本司，賜白藤肩輿，召至便殿勉諭。

translations.literal: In the second year, rising in the morning he fell on the steps and injured his right arm. On leave, within ten days he thrice submitted memorials resigning the chief ministership; the Zhou founder did not consent, exempted him from court attendance, had him conduct affairs in his own office, bestowed a white-rattan sedan chair, and summoned him to the side hall to encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: In his second year in office he fell down the steps one morning and injured his right arm. While on sick leave he three times within ten days asked to resign as chief minister; the Zhou founder refused, excused him from court attendance, had him work from his own office, gave him a white-rattan sedan chair, and summoned him to the side hall to urge him on.

sentences.zh: 穀不得已，起視事。

translations.literal: Gu had no choice but to rise and attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gu had no choice but to return to duty.

sentences.zh: 征兗州，為東京留守、判開封府事。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Yanzhou he served as eastern-capital regent and administrator of Kaifeng affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Yanzhou he served as regent of the eastern capital and administrator of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，加右僕射、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was given the additional titles of Right Vice Director and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xiande era he was made Right Vice Director and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.

sentences.zh: 從世宗征太原，遇賊於高平，匿山谷中，信宿而出，追及乘輿，世宗慰撫之。

translations.literal: Following Shizong on the campaign against Taiyuan, he encountered the enemy at Gaoping, hid in a mountain valley, emerged after two nights, caught up with the imperial carriage, and Shizong comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying Shizong on the Taiyuan campaign, he ran into the enemy at Gaoping, hid in a mountain valley for two nights, then rejoined the imperial train. Shizong comforted him warmly.

sentences.zh: 世宗將趨太原，命穀先調兵食，又代符彥卿判太原行府事。

translations.literal: When Shizong was about to press on to Taiyuan, he ordered Gu to arrange troops and provisions first, and also to replace Fu Yanqing as administrator of the Taiyuan campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: As Shizong prepared to advance on Taiyuan, he ordered Gu to arrange troops and supplies first and to replace Fu Yanqing as administrator of the Taiyuan campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 師還，進位司空、門下侍郎，監修國史。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was advanced to Grandee of Works and Vice Director of the Chancellery, and supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was promoted to Grandee of Works and Vice Director of the Chancellery, with charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 穀以史氏所述本於起居注，喪亂以來遂廢其職，上言請令端明、樞密直學士編記言動，為內廷日曆，以付史官。

translations.literal: Gu held that what the historians recorded derived from the diary of attendance and conduct, but since the disorders that office had been abandoned. He submitted a memorial requesting that Duanming and Privy Council academician-directors compile records of words and deeds as an inner-court calendar to hand to the historians.
translations.idiomatic: Gu argued that historical writing depended on the diary of attendance and conduct, an office abandoned since the civil wars. He memorialized that Duanming and Privy Council academician-directors should compile a record of imperial words and deeds as an inner-court calendar for the historians.

sentences.zh: 是歲，河大決齊、鄆，發十數州丁壯塞之，命穀領護，刻期就功。

translations.literal: That year the Yellow River burst its banks greatly in Qi and Yun; corvée laborers from more than ten prefectures were mobilized to block it. Gu was ordered to oversee the work, with a fixed deadline for completion.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Yellow River broke through catastrophically in Qi and Yun. Laborers from more than ten prefectures were mobilized for the repairs, and Gu was put in charge with a fixed deadline.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，議伐南唐，以穀為淮南道行營前軍都部署，兼知廬、壽等州行府事，忠武軍節度王彥副之，韓令坤以下十二將率從。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year they deliberated attacking Southern Tang. Gu was made overall commander of the vanguard of the Huainan campaign headquarters, and concurrently administrator of the campaign offices of Lu, Shou, and other prefectures. Wang Yan, military commissioner of Zhongwu, was his deputy, and twelve generals including Han Lingkun followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year the court debated war against Southern Tang. Gu was made overall commander of the Huainan vanguard and concurrently administrator of the campaign offices at Lu, Shou, and other prefectures. Wang Yan of Zhongwu served as his deputy, with twelve generals including Han Lingkun under his command.

sentences.zh: 穀領兵自正陽渡淮，先鋒都將白延遇敗吳軍數千於來遠，又破千餘人於山口鎮，進攻上窯，又敗千餘眾，獲其小校數十人，長圍壽春。

translations.literal: Gu led troops across the Huai from Zhengyang. The vanguard commander Bai Yanyu defeated several thousand Wu troops at Laiyuan, broke more than a thousand at Shankou town, advanced against Shangyao, defeated another thousand-odd, captured several dozen of their junior officers, and laid a long siege to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Gu led his army across the Huai from Zhengyang. Vanguard commander Bai Yanyu routed several thousand Wu troops at Laiyuan, destroyed another thousand at Shankou, took Shangyao after defeating a further thousand, captured dozens of enemy officers, and settled in for a long siege of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 南唐遣大將劉彥貞來援，穀召將佐謀曰：“今援軍已過來遠，距壽陽二百里，舟棹將及正陽。

translations.literal: Southern Tang sent the great general Liu Yanzhen to relieve the city. Gu summoned his officers and staff to deliberate, saying, "The relief army has already passed Laiyuan and is two hundred li from Shouyang; their boats will soon reach Zhengyang."
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang sent the great general Liu Yanzhen to relieve the siege. Gu called his officers together and said, "The relief force has already passed Laiyuan and is two hundred li from Shouyang; their fleet will soon reach Zhengyang."

sentences.zh: 我師無水戰之備，萬一斷橋梁，隔絕王師，則腹背受敵矣。

translations.literal: Our army has no preparation for naval combat. If they should cut the bridges and isolate the imperial army, we will be attacked front and rear."
translations.idiomatic: Our troops are not prepared for naval fighting. If they cut the bridges and cut off the imperial army, we will be caught between two enemies.

sentences.zh: 不如退守浮梁，以待戎輅之至。”

translations.literal: It would be better to withdraw and hold Fuliang, awaiting the arrival of the war chariot."
translations.idiomatic: We had better fall back to Fuliang and wait for the emperor to arrive.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗至圉鎮，已聞此謀，亟走內侍乘驛止之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shizong reached Yuan town, he had already heard of this plan and urgently sent a eunuch by post relay to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had already heard of this plan when he reached Yuan town and urgently sent a eunuch by relay post to forbid it.

sentences.zh: 穀已退保正陽，仍焚芻糧，回軍之際，遞相掠奪，淮北役夫數百悉陷於壽春。

translations.literal: Gu had already withdrawn to hold Zhengyang and still burned fodder and grain. On the retreat the troops plundered one another in turn, and several hundred corvée laborers north of the Huai all fell into Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Gu had already fallen back to Zhengyang and burned fodder and grain. During the retreat the troops looted one another, and several hundred laborers north of the Huai were captured at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞之怒，亟命李重進率師伐之，以穀判壽州行府。

translations.literal: When Shizong heard of it he was angry and urgently ordered Li Chongjin to lead troops to attack, appointing Gu administrator of the Shouzhou campaign office.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was furious when he heard and immediately ordered Li Chongjin to lead an attack, with Gu as administrator of the Shouzhou campaign office.

sentences.zh: 是秋，詔歸闕，得風痹疾，告滿百日，累表請致仕，優詔不允。

translations.literal: That autumn an edict recalled him to court. He contracted wind-paralysis illness; when his leave reached a hundred days he repeatedly submitted memorials requesting retirement, but gracious edicts did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was recalled to court. He developed rheumatic paralysis; when his sick leave reached a hundred days he repeatedly asked to retire, but the emperor's gracious edicts refused.

sentences.zh: 每軍國大事，令中使就第問之。

translations.literal: Whenever there were great affairs of state or army, he ordered palace envoys to go to his residence and inquire.
translations.idiomatic: On every major military or state matter, palace envoys were sent to his home to consult him.

sentences.zh: 四年春，吳人壁紫金山，築甬道以援壽春，不及者數里。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year the Wu entrenched on Purple Gold Mountain and built a covered way to relieve Shouchun, falling short by several li.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year the Wu fortified Purple Gold Mountain and built a covered approach to relieve Shouchun, stopping several li short.

sentences.zh: 師老無功，時請罷兵為便，世宗令范質、王溥就穀謀之。

translations.literal: The army was weary without achievement, and at the time many urged that ceasing hostilities would be advantageous. Shizong ordered Fan Zhi and Wang Pu to go to Gu to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The army was exhausted with little to show for it, and many urged withdrawal. Shizong sent Fan Zhi and Wang Pu to consult Gu.

sentences.zh: 穀手疏請親征，有必勝之利者三，世宗大悅，用其策。

translations.literal: Gu wrote in his own hand a memorial requesting a personal campaign, setting forth three advantages of certain victory. Shizong was greatly pleased and adopted his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu wrote in his own hand urging a personal campaign and listed three reasons for certain victory. Shizong was delighted and adopted his plan.

sentences.zh: 及淮南平，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified, rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan was pacified, his rewards were lavish.

sentences.zh: 出穀疏，令翰林學士承旨陶穀為讚以賜之。

translations.literal: Gu's memorial was published, and Hanlin academician-expositor Tao Gu was ordered to compose a laudation to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu's memorial was published, and Hanlin expositor Tao Gu was commissioned to write a laudatory inscription as a gift.

sentences.zh: 是夏，世宗還，穀扶疾見便殿，詔令不拜，命坐御坐側。

translations.literal: That summer Shizong returned. Gu, supporting himself through illness, was received in the side hall; an edict ordered that he not bow, and he was told to sit beside the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Shizong returned. Gu, leaning on attendants through illness, was received in the side hall, excused from bowing, and seated beside the throne.

sentences.zh: 以抱疾既久，請辭相位。

translations.literal: Because he had long been ill, he requested to resign the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Having been ill for so long, he asked to resign as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 世宗怡然勉之，謂曰：“譬如家有四子，一人有疾，棄而不養，非父之道也。

translations.literal: Shizong cheerfully encouraged him and said, "It is as if a household has four sons and one is ill— to abandon and not nurture him is not the way of a father."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong cheerfully urged him on and said, "Suppose a household has four sons and one falls ill— to cast him aside and refuse to care for him is no way for a father to act."

sentences.zh: 朕君臨萬方，卿處輔相之位，君臣之間，分義斯在，奈何以祿奉為言。”

translations.literal: I rule the myriad regions; you occupy the position of chief minister. Between lord and minister the allotment of duty lies here— why speak of salary and stipend?"
translations.idiomatic: I rule the realm; you hold the post of chief minister. Between us the bond of ruler and minister still holds— why talk of salary and stipend?

sentences.zh: 穀愧謝而退。

translations.literal: Gu withdrew in shame and thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Gu withdrew, ashamed and grateful.

sentences.zh: 俄以平壽州，敘功加爵邑。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, for the pacification of Shouzhou, his merit was reckoned and noble rank and fief increased.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for the capture of Shouzhou, his merit was recognized with added noble rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 是秋，穀抗表乞骸骨，罷相，守司空，加邑封，令每月肩輿一詣便殿，訪以政事。

translations.literal: That autumn Gu firmly submitted a memorial begging to surrender his bones. He was removed as chief minister but retained Grandee of Works, with increased fief; he was ordered once a month to come by sedan chair to the side hall to be consulted on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Gu firmly asked to retire. He left the chief ministership but kept the title Grandee of Works with an enlarged fief, and was told to come once a month by sedan chair to the side hall for consultation on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，世宗平淮南回，賜穀錢百萬、米麥五百斛、芻粟薪炭等。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year, when Shizong returned after pacifying Huainan, he bestowed on Gu a million in cash, five hundred hu of rice and wheat, and fodder, grain, firewood, and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year, when Shizong returned from pacifying Huainan, he gave Gu a million in cash, five hundred hu of grain, and supplies of fodder, fuel, and charcoal.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，加開府儀同三司，進封趙國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Gu was given the additional title of Grand Preceptor with ceremonial equal to the Three Dukes and advanced in fief to Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Gu was made Grand Preceptor with ceremonial equal to the Three Dukes and advanced to Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 求歸洛邑，賜錢三十萬，從其請。

translations.literal: He requested to return to Luoyang; three hundred thousand in cash was bestowed and his request granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to return to Luoyang; the court gave him three hundred thousand in cash and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，遣使就賜器幣。

translations.literal: When the Taizu of Song succeeded, envoys were sent to bestow vessels and silks at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu of Song took the throne, envoys were sent to his home with gifts of vessels and silks.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年，卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianlong he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 1 he died at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之震悼，贈侍中。

translations.literal: When Taizu heard of it he was shaken with grief and posthumously bestowed the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was deeply shaken when he heard and posthumously made him Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 穀為人厚重剛毅，深沉有城府，雅善談論，議政事能近取譬，言多詣理，辭氣明暢，人主為之聳聽。

translations.literal: Gu as a man was weighty, steady, firm, and resolute, deep and resourceful. He was skilled at elegant discourse; in discussing government affairs he could draw comparisons from what was near, his words mostly hit the principle, his diction clear and flowing, and the sovereign would listen with rapt attention.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was grave, steadfast, and resolute, deep-minded and shrewd. He spoke eloquently on affairs of state, drawing apt comparisons from everyday life; his reasoning was sound, his language clear, and rulers listened with rapt attention.

sentences.zh: 人有難必救，有恩必報。

translations.literal: When others were in difficulty he always rescued them; when he received favor he always repaid it.
translations.idiomatic: He always helped those in trouble and always repaid a kindness.

sentences.zh: 好汲引寒士，多至顯位。

translations.literal: He delighted in drawing up poor scholars, many of whom reached eminent positions.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in promoting poor scholars, many of whom rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 與韓熙載善，熙載將南渡，密告穀曰：“若江東相我，我當長驅以定中原。”

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Han Xizai. When Xizai was about to cross south, he secretly told Gu, "If the lands east of the Yangtze make me chief minister, I shall drive far north to settle the Central Plains."
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Han Xizai. When Xizai was about to flee south, he confided to Gu, "If the south makes me chief minister, I will march north and conquer the Central Plains."

sentences.zh: 穀笑曰：“若中原相我，下江南探囊中物耳。”

translations.literal: Gu laughed and said, "If the Central Plains make me chief minister, going down to Jiangnan will be like taking something from a bag at one's waist."
translations.idiomatic: Gu laughed and said, "If the north makes me chief minister, taking Jiangnan will be like reaching into one's own purse."

sentences.zh: 穀後果如其言。

translations.literal: Gu later proved exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Gu's words later proved exactly true.

sentences.zh: 李昉嘗為穀記室，在淮上被病求先歸。

translations.literal: Li Fang had once been Gu's secretariat officer. On the Huai he fell ill and asked to return ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang had once served as Gu's secretariat officer. While on the Huai he fell ill and asked to return home early.

sentences.zh: 穀視之曰：“子他日官祿當如我。”

translations.literal: Gu looked at him and said, "One day your office and emolument will be like mine."
translations.idiomatic: Gu looked at him and said, "One day your rank and salary will match mine."

sentences.zh: 昉後至宰相、司空。

translations.literal: Fang later reached chief minister and Grandee of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Fang later rose to chief minister and Grandee of Works.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，扈載以文章馳名，樞密使王樸薦令知制誥。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou, Hu Zai was famed for his literary compositions. Privy Council commissioner Wang Pu recommended him for drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande era of Later Zhou, Hu Zai was famed for his writing. Privy Council commissioner Wang Pu recommended him for drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 除書未下，樸詣中書言之。

translations.literal: Before the appointment edict was issued, Pu went to the Secretariat to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Before the appointment edict was issued, Pu went to the Secretariat to discuss it.

sentences.zh: 穀曰：“斯人薄命，慮不克享耳。”

translations.literal: Gu said, "This man's fate is thin; I fear he will not be able to enjoy it."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "That man has thin fortune—I doubt he will live to enjoy the post."

sentences.zh: 樸曰：“公在衡石之地，當以材進人，何得言命而遺才。”

translations.literal: Pu said, "You stand in the place of the balance and stone; you ought to advance people by talent— how can you speak of fate and leave talent behind?"
translations.idiomatic: Pu said, "You hold the scales of office—you should promote men for talent. How can you speak of fate and abandon ability?"

sentences.zh: 載遂知制誥，遷翰林學士，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Zai then took charge of drafting edicts, was transferred to Hanlin academician, and before long died.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was appointed to draft edicts, promoted to Hanlin academician, and died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 世謂樸能薦士，穀能知人。

translations.literal: The age said that Pu could recommend scholars and that Gu could know men.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time said that Wang Pu had a gift for recommending talent and that Li Gu had a gift for judging character.

sentences.zh: 穀歸洛中，昭義李筠以穀周朝名相，遺錢五十萬，他物稱是，穀受之。

translations.literal: When Gu returned to Luoyang, Li Jun of Zhaoyi, because Gu was a famed minister of the Zhou court, sent him five hundred thousand in cash and other goods in like measure; Gu accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Gu retired to Luoyang, Li Jun of Zhaoyi Circuit, taking him for a celebrated minister of the Later Zhou court, sent him five hundred thousand cash and comparable gifts in kind, and Gu accepted them.

sentences.zh: 既而筠叛，穀憂恚而終。

translations.literal: Before long Jun rebelled, and Gu died of grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Li Jun rebelled, and Li Gu died of grief and distress.

sentences.zh: 子吉至補闕，拱至太子中允。

translations.literal: His son Ji reached Reminder; Gong reached Junior Mentor in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji rose to Reminder, and Gong rose to Junior Mentor in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 昝居潤

translations.literal: Zan Jurun
translations.idiomatic: Zan Jurun

sentences.zh: 昝居潤，博州高唐人。

translations.literal: Zan Jurun was a native of Gaotang in Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zan Jurun came from Gaotang in Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 善書計。

translations.literal: He was skilled at writing and accounting.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at writing and bookkeeping.

sentences.zh: 後唐長興中，隸樞密院為小吏，以謹願稱。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era of Later Tang he was attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs as a minor clerk and was known for caution and sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing era of Later Tang he served in the Bureau of Military Affairs as a junior clerk and was known for his careful and conscientious manner.

sentences.zh: 晉初，出掌滑州廩庾，遂補牙職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin he went out to manage the grain storehouse of Hua Prefecture and was then appointed to a yamen staff post.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Later Jin he was sent out to manage the grain storehouse of Hua Prefecture and was then appointed to a staff post in the prefectural yamen.

sentences.zh: 會景延廣留守西洛，署為右職。

translations.literal: When Jing Yanyuan was left to guard western Luoyang, he appointed Jurun to a senior post on the right.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Yanyuan was left in charge of western Luoyang, he appointed Jurun to a senior post on his staff.

sentences.zh: 延廣卒，居潤往依陝帥白文珂，文珂致仕，乃表薦居潤於周祖。

translations.literal: When Yanyuan died, Jurun went to rely on Bai Wenke, military commissioner of Shaan, and when Wenke retired from office he submitted a memorial recommending Jurun to the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanyuan died, Jurun went to serve under Bai Wenke, military commissioner of Shaan Circuit. When Wenke retired, he submitted a memorial recommending Jurun to the founder of Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖立，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When the Taizu emperor was established, Jurun was given the additional title of Grand Preceptor with nominal commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu took the throne, Jurun was given the additional honorary title of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 及征澤、潞，命赴澶州巡警。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Ze and Lu was launched, he was ordered to go to Chanyang to patrol and keep watch.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Ze and Lu, he was ordered to Chanyang to patrol and maintain security.

sentences.zh: 師還，權知鎮州，加左領軍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was made acting prefect of Zhen Prefecture and given the additional title of General-in-Chief of the Left Metropolitan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he was appointed acting prefect of Zhen Prefecture and given the additional title of General-in-Chief of the Left Metropolitan Guard.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，又權知澶州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was again made acting prefect of Chanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2 he was again appointed acting prefect of Chanyang.

sentences.zh: 八月，拜義武軍節度，在鎮數年，得風痹，詔還京師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was appointed military governor of the Yiwu Army; after several years in the province he contracted wind paralysis, and an edict recalled him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was appointed military governor of the Yiwu Army. After several years in the province he developed rheumatic paralysis, and an edict recalled him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，卒，年五十九，贈太師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande he died at age fifty-nine and was posthumously given the title Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 4 he died at the age of fifty-nine and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 居潤性明敏，有節概，篤於行義。

translations.literal: Jurun was by nature bright and quick, possessed moral fiber, and was devoted to righteous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Jurun was bright and quick by nature, possessed moral fiber, and was deeply committed to doing what was right.

sentences.zh: 初，晉室將亡，景延廣委其族自洛赴難，至則為遼人所執。

translations.literal: At first, when the Jin house was near collapse, Jing Yanyuan sent his clan from Luoyang to answer the crisis, but on arrival they were seized by the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Later Jin regime was on the verge of collapse, Jing Yanyuan sent his family from Luoyang to answer the crisis, but on arrival they were seized by the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 遼人在洛者遽欲恣摽掠，延廣僚吏部曲悉遁，獨居潤力保護，其家以安。

translations.literal: The Liao in Luoyang at once wished to plunder at will; Yanyuan's staff officers and followers all fled, and Jurun alone exerted himself to protect them, so that the family was kept safe.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan in Luoyang at once set about plundering at will. Yanyuan's staff and followers all fled, but Jurun alone stood firm in their defense, and the family was kept safe.

sentences.zh: 居潤與太祖同事世宗，情好款浹，嘗薦沈倫於太祖，以為純謹可用，後至宰相，世稱其知人。

translations.literal: Jurun and the Taizu emperor had served Shizong together, and their friendship was warm and close. He once recommended Shen Lun to the Taizu emperor, deeming him pure, careful, and fit for use; Shen later reached chief minister, and the age praised Jurun for knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: Jurun and Emperor Taizu had served under Emperor Shizong together, and their friendship was warm and close. He once recommended Shen Lun to Taizu as a man of pure and careful character who could be trusted; Shen later rose to chief minister, and people praised Jurun for knowing men.

sentences.zh: 子惟質至內園使，弟居濟至水部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Weizhi reached Director of the Inner Park, and his younger brother Juji reached Vice Director of the Waterworks Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His son Weizhi rose to Director of the Inner Park, and his younger brother Juji rose to Vice Director of the Waterworks Bureau.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，錄其孫建中為三班借職。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu his grandson Jianzhong was enrolled in a provisional third-rank military post.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 3 his grandson Jianzhong was granted a provisional third-rank military appointment.

sentences.zh: 竇貞固

translations.literal: Dou Zhengu
translations.idiomatic: Dou Zhengu

sentences.zh: 天福三年，詔百僚各上封事，貞固疏曰：“臣聞舉善為明，知人則哲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu an edict ordered all officials each to submit a sealed memorial. Zhengu memorialized, saying, "Your servant has heard that to promote the good is to be enlightened and that to know men is to be wise.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 3 an edict ordered every official to submit a sealed memorial. Zhengu wrote, "I have heard that promoting the good is the mark of an enlightened ruler and knowing men the mark of a wise one.

sentences.zh: 聖君在位，藪澤豈有隱淪；

translations.literal: When a sage ruler holds the throne, how can marshes and lakes hide the submerged and obscure?
translations.idiomatic: When a sage ruler sits on the throne, how can talent remain hidden in the marshes and wilds?

sentences.zh: 昭代用材，政理固無紊亂。

translations.literal: In an enlightened age that employs talent, governance is naturally without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In an enlightened age that puts talent to use, government is naturally free of disorder.

sentences.zh: 求賢若渴，從諫如流，鄭所以譽子皮；

translations.literal: Thirsting for the worthy as for water and receiving remonstrance as a flowing stream—therefore Zheng praised Zi Pi;
translations.idiomatic: Thirsting for talent as for water and receiving remonstrance as a flowing stream—that is why the state of Zheng praised Zi Pi;

sentences.zh: 囗囗囗囗，囗囗囗囗，魯所以譏文仲。

translations.literal: [text illegible], [text illegible], therefore Lu criticized Wen Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: [text illegible], [text illegible]—that is why the state of Lu scorned Wen Zhong.

sentences.zh: 為國之要，進賢是先。

translations.literal: The essential point in governing a state is that advancing the worthy comes first.
translations.idiomatic: The first duty of governing a state is to advance worthy men.

sentences.zh: 陛下方樹丕基，宜求多士。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just now establishing a great foundation and ought to seek many scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is just now laying a great foundation and ought to seek out many men of talent.

sentences.zh: 乞降詔百僚，令各司議定一人，有何能識，堪何職官，朝廷依奏用之。

translations.literal: I beg that an edict be issued to all officials ordering each department to deliberate and settle on one man, stating what abilities and insight he possesses and what office he is fit for, so that the court may appoint him according to the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty issue an edict to all officials, directing each department to select one man after deliberation, set out his abilities and insight, and state what office he is fit to hold, so that the court may appoint him as recommended.

sentences.zh: 若能符薦引，果謂當才，所奏之官，望加獎賞；

translations.literal: If the recommendation proves true and the man recommended is indeed fit, I hope the recommending official may be rewarded;
translations.idiomatic: If the recommendation proves accurate and the man is truly fit for office, the official who submitted the recommendation should be rewarded;

sentences.zh: 如乖其舉，或涉徇私，所奏之官，宜加黜罰。

translations.literal: if it departs from the recommendation or involves favoritism, the recommending official ought to be demoted or punished.
translations.idiomatic: if the recommendation misses the mark or involves favoritism, the official who submitted it should be demoted or punished.

sentences.zh: 自然官由德序，位以才升。

translations.literal: Then naturally offices will follow virtue in order and rank will rise with talent.
translations.idiomatic: Then offices will naturally be ordered by virtue and rank will rise with talent.

sentences.zh: 三人同行，尚聞擇善；

translations.literal: When three men walk together, one still hears of choosing the good;
translations.idiomatic: Even when three men walk together, one still hears of choosing the good;

sentences.zh: 十目所視，必不濫知。

translations.literal: what ten eyes behold will certainly not be known at random.
translations.idiomatic: what ten eyes behold will certainly not be judged carelessly.

sentences.zh: 臣職在論思，敢陳狂狷。”

translations.literal: Your servant's duty lies in deliberation and reflection, and I dare present this forthright but narrow-minded counsel."
translations.idiomatic: My duty is to deliberate and advise, and I venture to offer this blunt counsel."

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝深嘉之，命所司著為令典。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor greatly praised it and ordered the responsible office to set it down as an established regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor greatly praised it and ordered the appropriate office to codify it as a standing regulation.

sentences.zh: 明年，改御史中丞，與太常卿崔棁、刑部侍郎呂琦、禮部侍郎張允同詳定正冬朝會禮節、樂章及二舞行列。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief and, together with Grandee of Ceremonies Cui Shuai, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, and Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, worked out in detail the rites of the winter court assembly, the musical sections, and the formations of the two dances.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Censor-in-Chief and, together with Grandee of Ceremonies Cui Shuai, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, and Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, worked out the rites of the winter court assembly, the musical sections, and the formations of the two ritual dances.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部、門下二侍郎。

translations.literal: He passed through the two vice ministries of Justice and of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Vice Minister of Justice and Vice Minister of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor acceded, Zhengu was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor acceded to the throne, Zhengu was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書，知貢舉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites and put in charge of the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Rites and put in charge of the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 舊制，進士夜試，繼以三燭。

translations.literal: By the old system, jinshi candidates were examined at night and then given three candles.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, jinshi candidates were examined at night and allotted three candles.

sentences.zh: 長興二年改令晝試，貞固以晝晷短，難盡士材，奏復夜試。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changxing the rule was changed to daytime examination. Zhengu, because the daylight hours were short and made it hard to exhaust the candidates' talent, memorialized to restore the night examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing 2 the rule was changed to daytime examination. Zhengu argued that the daylight hours were too short to allow candidates to show their full ability and memorialized to restore the night examination.

sentences.zh: 擇士平允，時論稱之。

translations.literal: In selecting scholars he was fair and even, and opinion of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In selecting candidates he was fair and even-handed, and public opinion praised him.

sentences.zh: 改刑部尚書，出為潁州團練使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice and sent out as training commissioner of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Justice and sent out as training commissioner of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was again appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he was again appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入汴，貞固與禮部尚書王松率百官見於滎陽西，漢祖駐駕，勞問久之。

translations.literal: When the Han founder entered Bian, Zhengu and Minister of Rites Wang Song led the hundred officials to meet him west of Xingyang. The Han founder halted his carriage and questioned and consoled them at length.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder of Later Han entered Bian, Zhengu and Minister of Rites Wang Song led the hundred officials to meet him west of Xingyang. The founder halted his carriage and spoke with them at length in encouragement.

sentences.zh: 初營宗廟，帝以姓自漢出，遂襲國號，尊光武為始祖，並親廟為五。

translations.literal: When the ancestral temples were first being established, the emperor, because his surname came from Han, thereupon adopted that dynastic name, honored Guangwu as founding ancestor, and made the direct ancestral temples five in all.
translations.idiomatic: When the ancestral temples were first being established, the emperor, taking his surname from Han, adopted that dynastic name, honored Emperor Guangwu as founding ancestor, and set the direct ancestral temples at five.

sentences.zh: 詔群臣議，貞固上言曰：“按《王制》：‘天子七廟，諸侯五，大夫三，士一。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ministers to deliberate. Zhengu submitted, saying, "According to the Royal Regulations: 'The Son of Heaven has seven temples, feudal lords five, grandees three, and officers one.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the ministers to deliberate. Zhengu submitted, "According to the Royal Regulations: 'The Son of Heaven has seven temples, feudal lords five, grandees three, and officers one.'

sentences.zh: ’《正義》曰：‘周之制七廟者，太祖及文王、武王之祧與親廟四也。

translations.literal: ' The Correct Meaning says: 'In the Zhou system of seven temples, there were the founding ancestor and the distant shrines of King Wen and King Wu together with four direct ancestral temples.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The Correct Meaning says: 'In the Zhou system of seven temples, there were the founding ancestor, the distant shrines of King Wen and King Wu, and four direct ancestral temples.'

sentences.zh: ’又曰：‘七廟者，據周也。

translations.literal: ' It also says: 'Seven temples refers to Zhou.'
translations.idiomatic: ' It also says: 'Seven temples refers to the Zhou model.'

sentences.zh: 有其人則七，無其人則五。

translations.literal: ' When there are such men there are seven; when there are not, there are five.'
translations.idiomatic: ' When there are such men there are seven; when there are not, there are five.'

sentences.zh: ’至光武中興，及魏、晉、宋、齊、隋、唐，或立六廟，或立四廟，蓋建國之始，未盈其數也。

translations.literal: ' Down to the restoration of Guangwu and through Wei, Jin, Song, Qi, Sui, and Tang, some established six temples and some four, for at the beginning of founding a state the full number had not yet been reached.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Down to the restoration of Guangwu and through Wei, Jin, Song, Qi, Sui, and Tang, some established six temples and some four, for at the founding of a state the full number had not yet been reached.'

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰‘德厚者流光’，此天子可以祀六世之義也。

translations.literal: The Rites say, 'Those of deep virtue leave lasting light,' and this is the sense in which a Son of Heaven may sacrifice to six generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say, 'Those of deep virtue leave lasting light,' and this is the sense in which a Son of Heaven may sacrifice to six generations.

sentences.zh: 今陛下大定寰區，重興漢祚，旁求典禮，用正宗祧，伏請立高、曾、祖、禰四親廟。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has greatly settled the realm, revived the Han fortune, and sought ritual on every side to use the correct main ancestral line. I humbly ask that four direct ancestral temples be established for the great-great-grandfather, great-grandfather, grandfather, and father.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has greatly settled the realm, revived the Han fortune, and sought ritual precedents on every side to establish the correct main ancestral line. I humbly ask that four direct ancestral temples be established for the great-great-grandfather, great-grandfather, grandfather, and father.

sentences.zh: 及自古聖王祖有功、宗有德、更立始祖在四廟之外，不拘定數，所以或五廟或七廟。

translations.literal: Moreover, from antiquity sage rulers have honored merit as founding ancestors and virtue as cult ancestors and have additionally established a founding ancestor outside the four temples, not bound by a fixed number; hence there were sometimes five temples and sometimes seven.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, from antiquity sage rulers have honored merit as founding ancestors and virtue as cult ancestors and have additionally established a founding ancestor outside the four temples, not bound by a fixed number; hence there were sometimes five temples and sometimes seven.

sentences.zh: 今請尊高皇帝、光武皇帝為始祖，法文王、武王不遷之制，用歷代六廟之規，庶合典禮。”

translations.literal: Now I ask that Emperor Gao and Emperor Guangwu be honored as founding ancestors, following the system by which King Wen and King Wu were immovable shrines and using the six-temple rule of successive dynasties, so that this may accord with ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Now I ask that Emperor Gao and Emperor Guangwu be honored as founding ancestors, following the system by which King Wen and King Wu were immovable shrines and adopting the six-temple rule of successive dynasties, so that this may accord with ritual."

sentences.zh: 漢祖從之。

translations.literal: The Han founder followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The founder of Later Han accepted this.

sentences.zh: 論者以天子建國，各從其所起，堯自唐侯，禹生大夏是也。

translations.literal: Critics held that when a Son of Heaven founded a state each traced his origin to where he arose: Yao from the Lord of Tang and Yu born in Great Xia were cases in point.
translations.idiomatic: Critics held that when a Son of Heaven founded a state he traced his origin to where he had risen: Yao from the Lord of Tang and Yu born in Great Xia were cases in point.

sentences.zh: 立廟皆祖其有功，商之契，周之後稷，魏之武帝，晉之三廟是也。

translations.literal: In establishing temples all took as ancestors those who had merit: Shang's Qi, Zhou's Hou Ji, Wei's Emperor Wu, and Jin's three temples were cases in point.
translations.idiomatic: In establishing temples all took as ancestors those who had merit: Shang's Qi, Zhou's Hou Ji, Wei's Emperor Wu, and Jin's three temples were cases in point.

sentences.zh: 高祖起於晉陽，而追嗣兩漢，徒以同姓為遠祖，甚非其義；

translations.literal: The High Ancestor rose at Jinyang yet traced succession to the two Han dynasties, taking a distant ancestor merely because the surname was the same—this was very much against the proper meaning;
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor rose at Jinyang yet traced succession to the two Han dynasties, taking distant ancestors merely because the surname was the same—this was very much against the proper meaning;

sentences.zh: 貞固又以四親匹庶，上合高、光，失之彌遠矣。

translations.literal: Zhengu further matched the four direct ancestors to commoners while joining them above with Gao and Guangwu, which missed the mark all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengu further matched the four direct ancestors to commoners while linking them above with Gao and Guangwu, which missed the mark all the more.

sentences.zh: 但援立親廟可也，餘皆非禮。

translations.literal: Only in citing the establishment of direct ancestral temples was he acceptable; the rest was all against ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Only in citing the establishment of direct ancestral temples was he acceptable; the rest was all against ritual.

sentences.zh: 俄遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 周祖兵起，貞固與蘇逢吉奉隱帝兵次於野，敗。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder raised troops, Zhengu and Su Fengji escorted the Hidden Emperor's army and halted in the field, but were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder of Later Zhou raised troops, Zhengu and Su Fengji escorted Emperor Yindi's army into the field, but they were defeated.

sentences.zh: 逢吉倉黃自殺，貞固遂詣周祖。

translations.literal: Fengji, in panic, killed himself, and Zhengu then went to the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji, in panic, killed himself, and Zhengu then went over to the Zhou founder.

sentences.zh: 周祖稱太后制，委貞固與蘇禹珪、王峻同掌軍國政事。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder, invoking an order of the empress dowager, entrusted Zhengu together with Su Yugui and Wang Jun to administer together the military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder, invoking an order of the empress dowager, entrusted Zhengu together with Su Yugui and Wang Jun to administer military and state affairs jointly.

sentences.zh: 周祖登位，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder ascended the throne, Zhengu was additionally given the concurrent title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder ascended the throne, Zhengu was additionally given the concurrent title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 會以馮道為首相，改監修國史。

translations.literal: When Feng Dao became chief minister, Zhengu was changed to Supervisor of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Dao became chief minister, Zhengu was reassigned as Supervisor of the National History.

sentences.zh: 俄罷相，守司徒，封沂國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was removed as chief minister, kept the title of Minister of Education, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was removed as chief minister, retained the title of Minister of Education, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，以范質為司徒，貞固遂歸洛陽，輸課役，齒為編民。

translations.literal: When Shizong acceded, Fan Zhi was made Minister of Education, and Zhengu then returned to Luoyang, paid taxes and corvée, and was counted as an ordinary registered citizen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded to the throne, Fan Zhi was made Minister of Education, and Zhengu returned to Luoyang, paid taxes and corvée labor, and was counted as an ordinary registered citizen.

sentences.zh: 貞固不能堪，訴於留守向拱，拱不聽。

translations.literal: Zhengu could not bear it and appealed to the left-behind commander Xiang Gong, but Gong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengu could not bear it and appealed to the left-behind commander Xiang Gong, but Gong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 宋初，以前三公赴闕陪位，詣范質，求任東宮三少，預朝請，質不為奏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, because of his former rank as one of the Three Excellencies he went to court to take his place in attendance. He called on Fan Zhi and asked to be appointed one of the three junior tutors of the Eastern Palace and to attend court audiences, but Zhi would not submit the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song, because of his former rank as one of the Three Excellencies he went to court to take his place in attendance. He called on Fan Zhi and asked to be appointed one of the three junior tutors of the Eastern Palace and to attend court audiences, but Zhi would not submit the memorial.

sentences.zh: 乃還洛，放曠山水，與布衣輩攜妓載酒以自適。

translations.literal: He then returned to Luoyang, gave himself over to mountains and streams, and with commoners took courtesans and wine for his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to Luoyang, gave himself over to mountains and streams, and with commoners took courtesans and wine for his pleasure.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年病困，自為墓誌，卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, gravely ill, he wrote his own epitaph and died at age seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 2, gravely ill, he wrote his own epitaph and died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 李濤，字信臣，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Li Tao, courtesy name Xinchen, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tao, whose courtesy name was Xinchen, came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 唐敬宗子郇王瑋十世孫。

translations.literal: He was a tenth-generation descendant of Prince of Xun, Wei, son of Emperor Jingzong of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He was a tenth-generation descendant of Prince Wei of Xun, son of Emperor Jingzong of Tang.

sentences.zh: 祖鎮，臨濮令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was magistrate of Linpu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen was magistrate of Linpu.

sentences.zh: 父元，將作監。

translations.literal: His father Yuan was Director of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan was Director of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 朱梁革命，元以宗室懼禍，挈濤避地湖南，依馬殷，署濤衡陽令。

translations.literal: When the Zhu dynasty replaced Tang, Yuan, as a member of the imperial clan, feared disaster, took Tao and fled to Hunan, relied on Ma Yin, and had Tao appointed magistrate of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Liang replaced Tang, Yuan, as a member of the imperial clan, feared disaster, took Tao and fled to Hunan, placed himself under Ma Yin, and had Tao appointed magistrate of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 濤從父兄郁仕梁為閣門使，上言濤父子旅湖湘，詔殷遣歸京師，補河陽令。

translations.literal: Tao's older male cousin Yu served the Liang as Gate Commissioner and submitted that Tao and his father were sojourning in Hunan and Hubei. An edict ordered Yin to send them back to the capital, and Tao was appointed magistrate of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's older male cousin Yu served the Liang as Gate Commissioner and reported that Tao and his father were living in exile in Hunan and Hubei. An edict ordered Yin to send them back to the capital, and Tao was appointed magistrate of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成初，舉進士甲科，自晉州從事拜監察御史，遷右補闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng in Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination in the top class, was promoted from aide in Jin Prefecture to Investigating Censor, and was transferred to Remonstrance and Advice on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tiancheng in Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination in the top class, was promoted from aide in Jin Prefecture to Investigating Censor, and was transferred to Remonstrance and Advice on the Right.

sentences.zh: 宋王從厚鎮鄴，以濤為魏博觀察判官。

translations.literal: When Song Wang Conghou governed Ye, Tao was made administrative aide of the Weibo observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Wang Conghou governed Ye, Tao was made administrative aide of the Weibo observation commission.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，入為起居舍人。

translations.literal: After more than a year he entered court as Drafting Secretary in Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he entered court service as Drafting Secretary in Attendance.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，改考功員外郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu in Jin he was changed to Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations and compiler in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianfu in Later Jin he was made Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations and compiler in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 晉祖幸大梁，張從賞以盟津叛，陷洛陽，扼虎牢。

translations.literal: When the Jin founder visited Daliang, Zhang Congshang rebelled at the Mengjin crossing, captured Luoyang, and seized Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin founder visited Daliang, Zhang Congshang rebelled at the Mengjin crossing, captured Luoyang, and seized Hulao Pass.

sentences.zh: 故齊王全義子張繼祚者實黨之，晉祖將族其家。

translations.literal: Zhang Jizuo, son of the former Prince of Qi, Quan Yi, was in fact his partisan, and the Jin founder was about to exterminate the family.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jizuo, son of the former Prince of Qi, Quan Yi, was in fact his partisan, and the Jin founder was about to exterminate the family.

sentences.zh: 濤上疏曰：“全義歷事累朝，頗著功效。

translations.literal: Tao submitted a memorial, saying, "Quan Yi served successive courts and achieved considerable merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tao submitted a memorial, saying, "Quan Yi served successive courts and achieved considerable merit.

sentences.zh: 當巢、蔡之亂，京師為墟，全義手披荊棘，再造都邑，垂五十年，洛民賴之。

translations.literal: During the disorders of Chao and Cai the capital became ruins; Quan Yi with his own hands cleared the brambles and rebuilt the city. For nearly fifty years the people of Luoyang relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: During the disorders of Chao and Cai the capital was reduced to ruins; Quan Yi with his own hands cleared the brambles and rebuilt the city. For nearly fifty years the people of Luoyang relied on him.

sentences.zh: 乞以全義之故，止罪繼祚妻子。”

translations.literal: I beg that for Quan Yi's sake punishment be limited to Jizuo's wife and children."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that for Quan Yi's sake punishment be limited to Jizuo's wife and children."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉詔為宋州括田使，前雄州刺史袁正辭齎束帛遺濤，以田園為託，濤表其事，晉祖嘉之。

translations.literal: He once received an edict to serve as land-survey commissioner of Song Prefecture. The former prefect of Xiong, Yuan Zhengci, brought silk gifts and presented them to Tao, entrusting his fields and gardens to him. Tao memorialized the matter, and the Jin founder praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He once received an edict to serve as land-survey commissioner of Song Prefecture. The former prefect of Xiong, Yuan Zhengci, brought silk gifts and presented them to Tao, asking him to look after his fields and gardens. Tao memorialized the matter, and the Jin founder praised him.

sentences.zh: 正辭坐降一階，濤遷浚儀令。

translations.literal: Zhengci was demoted one rank for it, and Tao was transferred to magistrate of Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengci was demoted one rank for it, and Tao was transferred to magistrate of Junyi.

sentences.zh: 改比部郎中、鹽判官，改刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He was changed to Director of the Bureau of Comparisons and salt commissioner aide, then changed to Director of the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Bureau of Comparisons and salt commissioner aide, then Director of the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 涇帥張彥澤殺記室張式，奪其妻，式家人詣闕上訴。

translations.literal: The military commissioner of Jing, Zhang Yanze, killed his secretary Zhang Shi and seized his wife. Shi's family went to court to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: The military commissioner of Jing Circuit, Zhang Yanze, killed his secretary Zhang Shi and seized his wife. Shi's family went to court to appeal.

sentences.zh: 晉祖以彥澤有軍功，釋其罪。

translations.literal: The Jin founder, because Yanze had military merit, released him from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder, because Yanze had military merit, released him from punishment.

sentences.zh: 濤伏閣抗疏，請置於法。

translations.literal: Tao prostrated himself at the palace gate and submitted a forceful memorial asking that Yanze be punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Tao prostrated himself at the palace gate and submitted a forceful memorial asking that Yanze be punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 晉祖召見諭之，濤植笏叩階，聲色俱厲，晉祖怒叱之，濤執笏如初。

translations.literal: The Jin founder summoned him and admonished him. Tao planted his tablet and knocked on the steps; his voice and expression were both stern. The Jin founder angrily shouted at him, but Tao held his tablet as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder summoned him and admonished him. Tao planted his tablet and knocked on the steps; his voice and expression were both stern. The Jin founder angrily shouted at him, but Tao held his tablet as before.

sentences.zh: 晉祖曰：“吾與彥澤有誓約，恕其死。”

translations.literal: The Jin founder said: "I have a sworn pact with Yanze; I pardon his death."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder said, "I have a sworn pact with Yanze; I pardon his life."

sentences.zh: 濤厲聲曰：“彥澤私誓，陛下不忍食其言；

translations.literal: Tao said in a harsh voice: "Yanze's private pledge—Your Majesty cannot bear to eat your word;
translations.idiomatic: Tao answered in a harsh voice: "That was Yanze's private pledge. Your Majesty cannot bear to go back on your word—

sentences.zh: 范延光嘗賜鐵券，今復安在？”

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang was once granted an iron certificate—where is it now?"
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang was once granted an iron certificate promising he would not be put to death—where is that now?"

sentences.zh: 晉祖不能答，即拂衣起，濤隨之，諫不已。

translations.literal: The Jin founder could not answer, immediately shook out his robes and rose; Tao followed him, remonstrating without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder had no reply. He shook out his robes and rose at once; Tao followed him and kept remonstrating without cease.

sentences.zh: 晉祖不得已，召式父鐸、弟守貞、子希範等皆拜以官，罷彥澤節製。

translations.literal: The Jin founder, having no choice, summoned Shi's father Duo, younger brother Shouzhen, son Xifan, and others, all invested with offices, and removed Yanze's military commission.
translations.idiomatic: When he could do nothing else, the Jin founder summoned Shi's father Duo, his younger brother Shouzhen, his son Xifan, and the rest, conferred offices on them all, and stripped Yanze of his military command.

sentences.zh: 濤歸洛下，賦詩自悼，有“三諫不從歸去來”之句。

translations.literal: Tao returned to Luoyang and composed a poem lamenting himself, with the line "Three remonstrances not followed—go back whence I came."
translations.idiomatic: Tao returned to Luoyang and wrote a poem of self-lament containing the line, "Three remonstrances unheeded—I return whence I came."

sentences.zh: 先是，范延光據鄴叛，晉祖賜鐵券許以不死，終亦不免，故濤引之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fan Yanguang held Ye in rebellion; the Jin founder granted an iron certificate vowing no death, yet in the end he was not spared—therefore Tao cited this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Fan Yanguang rebelled from Ye, the Jin founder had granted him an iron certificate of indemnity promising that he would not be executed, yet in the end that promise availed him nothing—hence Tao's allusion.

sentences.zh: 晉祖崩，濤坐不赴臨，停。

translations.literal: When the Jin founder died, Tao was punished for not attending the mourning audience and was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin founder died, Tao was punished for failing to attend the mourning rites and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起為洛陽令，遷屯田職方郎中、中書舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he was reappointed magistrate of Luoyang, then transferred to Director in the Bureaus of State Farms and Works and Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reappointed magistrate of Luoyang, then promoted to Director in the Bureaus of State Farms and Works and Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會契丹入汴，彥澤領突騎入京城，恣行殺害，人皆為濤危之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, Yanze led crack cavalry into the capital and wantonly killed; everyone feared for Tao's safety.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Bian, Yanze led crack cavalry into the capital and slaughtered at will; everyone feared for Tao's life.

sentences.zh: 濤詣其帳，通刺謁見。

translations.literal: Tao went to his tent and, presenting his calling card, requested an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Tao went to Yanze's tent, presented his calling card, and requested an audience.

sentences.zh: 彥澤曰：“舍人懼乎？”

translations.literal: Yanze said: "Secretariat Drafter, are you afraid?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanze said, "Secretariat Drafter, are you afraid?"

sentences.zh: 濤曰：“今日之懼，亦猶足下昔年之懼也。

translations.literal: Tao said: "The fear of today is also like the fear of you in years past.
translations.idiomatic: Tao said, "The fear I feel today is no different from the fear you felt back then.

sentences.zh: 向使先皇聽僕言，寧有今日之事。”

translations.literal: Had the late emperor listened to my words, how could there be today's affair?"
translations.idiomatic: Had the late emperor listened to me, how could today's events have come to pass?"

sentences.zh: 彥澤大笑，命酒對酌，濤神氣自若。

translations.literal: Yanze laughed loudly, ordered wine, and they drank facing each other; Tao's spirit and bearing were as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yanze laughed loudly, ordered wine, and they drank facing each other; Tao remained perfectly composed.

sentences.zh: 漢祖起義至洛，濤自汴奉百官表入對，漢祖問京師財賦，從契丹去後所存幾何，濤具對稱旨，漢祖嘉之。

translations.literal: When the Han founder raised his uprising and reached Luoyang, Tao came from Bian with the memorial of the hundred officials to audience; the Han founder asked about the capital's finances and how much remained after the Khitan departure; Tao answered fully to satisfaction, and the Han founder praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder raised his uprising and reached Luoyang, Tao came from Bian bearing the memorial of the hundred officials to audience. The Han founder asked about the capital's finances and how much remained after the Khitan withdrawal; Tao answered in full to his satisfaction, and the Han founder praised him.

sentences.zh: 至汴，以為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Bian he was made Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Bian he was appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 杜重威據鄴叛，高祖命高行周、慕容彥超討之，二帥不協。

translations.literal: When Du Chongwei rebelled holding Ye, Gaozu ordered Gao Xingzhou and Murong Yanchao to suppress him; the two commanders did not cooperate.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chongwei rebelled holding Ye, Gaozu ordered Gao Xingzhou and Murong Yanchao to suppress him, but the two commanders would not cooperate.

sentences.zh: 濤密疏請親征。

translations.literal: Tao submitted a secret memorial requesting a personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Tao submitted a secret memorial asking that the emperor lead the campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 高祖覽奏，以濤堪任宰輔，即拜中書侍郎兼戶部尚書、平章事。

translations.literal: Gaozu read the memorial and, deeming Tao fit for chief minister, at once appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Revenue, and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu read the memorial and, judging Tao fit for chief minister, at once appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Revenue, and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，楊邠、周祖共掌機密，史弘肇握兵柄，與武德使李鄴等中外爭權，互作威福。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yin acceded, Yang Bin and the Zhou founder jointly held secret affairs; Shi Hongzhao grasped military power and, with the Military Virtue envoy Li Ye and others, fought for power inside and outside court, each making authority and favor serve himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yin acceded, Yang Bin and the Zhou founder jointly controlled secret affairs; Shi Hongzhao held military power and, with the Military Virtue envoy Li Ye and others, vied for authority inside and outside the court, each wielding power for his own ends.

sentences.zh: 濤疏請出邠等藩鎮，以清朝政。

translations.literal: Tao submitted a memorial asking that Bin and the others be sent out to military governorships to clarify court government.
translations.idiomatic: Tao submitted a memorial asking that Bin and the others be sent out to provincial commands so that court government might be clarified.

sentences.zh: 隱帝不能決，白於太后，太后召邠等諭之，反為所構，免相歸第。

translations.literal: Emperor Yin could not decide; he informed the Empress Dowager, who summoned Bin and the others to instruct them—but instead was framed by them; Tao was removed as chancellor and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yin could not decide; he informed the Empress Dowager, who summoned Bin and the others to instruct them—but they turned the tables on her instead; Tao was dismissed as chancellor and sent home.

sentences.zh: 時中書廚釜鳴者數四，濤晝寢閣中，夢嚴飾廳事，群吏趨走，云迎新宰相帶諸司使，既寤，心異之。

translations.literal: At the time the cauldrons in the Secretariat kitchen rang four times; Tao napped in the office and dreamed of a richly adorned hall with clerks rushing about, saying a new chancellor was arriving with the various commissioner titles; when he awoke he thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the cauldrons in the Secretariat kitchen rang four times. Tao napped in the office and dreamed of a richly adorned hall where clerks rushed about, announcing that a new chancellor was arriving bearing the various commissioner titles. When he awoke he found it strange.

sentences.zh: 數日濤罷，以邠為相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: Within days Tao was dismissed, and Bin was made chancellor and concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Tao was dismissed, and Bin was made chancellor and concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 及周祖舉兵，太后倉皇涕泣曰：“不用李濤之言，宜其亡也。”

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder raised troops, the Empress Dowager in panic wept and said: "Had we not heeded Li Tao's words, this ruin was to be expected.
