translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder raised troops, the Empress Dowager wept in panic and said, "Had we not heeded Li Tao's counsel, this ruin was to be expected.

sentences.zh: 周初，起為太子賓客，歷刑部、戶部二尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou he was reappointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and successively served as Minister of Punishments and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhou he was reappointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and successively served as Minister of Punishments and Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 世宗宴駕，為山陵副使。

translations.literal: When Shizong died he served as deputy commissioner for the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong died he served as deputy commissioner for the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，封莒國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong acceded he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong acceded he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ju.

sentences.zh: 宋初，拜兵部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Song he was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，濤被病。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, Tao fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong, Tao fell ill.

sentences.zh: 有軍校尹勳董浚五丈河，陳留丁壯夜潰，勳擅斬隊長陳琲等十人，丁夫七十人皆杖一百，刵其左耳。

translations.literal: The army commander Yin Xun was supervising dredging of the Wuzhang River; the able-bodied men of Chenliu fled by night; Xun on his own authority executed the squad leaders Chen Pei and nine others, had seventy corvée laborers flogged a hundred strokes each, and branded their left ears.
translations.idiomatic: The army commander Yin Xun was supervising dredging of the Wuzhang River when the able-bodied men of Chenliu scattered by night. Xun on his own authority executed the squad leaders Chen Pei and nine others, had seventy corvée laborers flogged a hundred strokes each, and branded their left ears.

sentences.zh: 濤聞之，力疾草奏，請斬勳以謝百姓。

translations.literal: When Tao heard this he forced himself despite illness to draft a memorial requesting Xun's execution to appease the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao heard of this he forced himself, though ill, to draft a memorial asking that Xun be executed to appease the people.

sentences.zh: 家人謂濤曰：“公久病，宜自愛養，朝廷事且置之。”

translations.literal: His family said to Tao: "You have been ill for long; you should care for yourself and leave court affairs aside for now."
translations.idiomatic: His family said to Tao, "You have been ill a long time; you should look after yourself and leave court affairs aside for now."

sentences.zh: 濤憤言曰：“人孰無死，但我為兵部尚書，坐視軍校無辜殺人，烏得不奏？”

translations.literal: Tao said angrily: "Who does not die? But I am Minister of War—how can I sit by while an army commander kills people without cause and not memorialize?"
translations.idiomatic: Tao said angrily, "Who does not die? But I am Minister of War—how can I sit by while an army commander kills people without cause and not submit a memorial?"

sentences.zh: 太祖覽奏嘉之，詔削奪勳官爵，配隸許州。

translations.literal: Taizu read the memorial and praised it; an edict stripped Xun of rank and office and banished him as convict labor to Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu read the memorial and praised it; an edict stripped Xun of rank and office and banished him as convict labor to Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 濤卒，年六十四，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: Tao died at age sixty-four; he was posthumously given Vice Director of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Tao died at sixty-four and was posthumously given the title of Vice Director of the Left.

sentences.zh: 濤慷慨有大志，以經綸為己任。

translations.literal: Tao was magnanimous and ambitious, taking statecraft as his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was open-handed and ambitious, taking the ordering of the state as his personal charge.

sentences.zh: 工為詩，筆劄遒媚，性滑稽，善諧謔，亦未嘗忤物，居家以孝友聞。

translations.literal: He was skilled at poetry; his letters were vigorous and elegant; his nature was humorous and he was good at witty banter, yet he never gave offense; at home he was known for filial piety and brotherly kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at poetry and wrote letters of vigorous elegance. His nature was humorous and he excelled at witty banter, yet he never gave offense; at home he was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，其孫惟勤詣闕自陳，詔授許州司士參軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde, his grandson Wei Qin came to court to petition in person; an edict appointed him Registrar in Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingde, his grandson Wei Qin came to court to petition in person and was appointed by edict Registrar in Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子承休至尚書水部郎中，承休子仲容。

translations.literal: His son Chenghua rose to Director in the Ministry of Works' Water Bureau; Chenghua's son was Zhongrong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chenghua rose to Director in the Ministry of Works' Water Bureau; Chenghua's son was Zhongrong.

sentences.zh: 弟 澣

translations.literal: Younger brother Huan
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother Huan

sentences.zh: 濤弟澣，字日新。

translations.literal: Tao's younger brother Huan, courtesy name Rixin.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's younger brother Huan, whose courtesy name was Rixin.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏，慕王、楊、盧、駱為文章。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever; he admired Wang, Yang, Lu, and Luo as masters of prose.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and took Wang, Yang, Lu, and Luo as models in prose.

sentences.zh: 後唐長興初，吳越王錢騑卒，詔兵部侍郎楊凝式撰神道碑，令澣代草，凡萬餘言，文彩遒麗，時輩稱之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changxing in Later Tang, when King Qian of Wu-Yue died, an edict ordered Vice Minister of War Yang Ningshi to compose a spirit-way stele inscription; Huan was ordered to draft it in his stead—more than ten thousand characters in all, its literary color vigorous and elegant, and contemporaries praised it.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Changxing in Later Tang, when Qian Liu, King of Wu-Yue, died, an edict ordered Vice Minister of War Yang Ningshi to compose a spirit-way stele inscription; Huan was ordered to draft it in his place. The text ran to more than ten thousand characters, its literary color vigorous and elegant, and contemporaries praised it.

sentences.zh: 秦王從榮召至幕中，從榮敗，勒歸田里。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the staff of Prince of Qin Congrong; when Congrong was defeated he was compelled to return to his village.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the staff of the Prince of Qin, Congrong; when Congrong was defeated he was compelled to return to his village.

sentences.zh: 久之，起為校書郎、集賢校理。

translations.literal: After a long time he was reappointed Proofreader and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was reappointed Proofreader and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，拜右拾遺，俄召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he was appointed Remonstrance and Review on the Right, and soon after summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianfu era of Later Jin he was appointed Remonstrance and Review on the Right, and soon after was summoned as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 會廢學士院，出為吏部員外郎，遷禮部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: When the Hanlin Academy was abolished he went out as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then transferred to Director in the Ministry of Rites and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hanlin Academy was abolished he was sent out as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then transferred to Director in the Ministry of Rites and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 復置翰林，遷中書舍人，再為學士。

translations.literal: When the Hanlin was restored he was transferred to Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat and again served as Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hanlin was restored he was transferred to Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat and again served as Academician.

sentences.zh: 時濤在西掖，縉紳榮之。

translations.literal: At the time Tao was in the western secretariat; the gentry considered it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Tao served in the western secretariat; the gentry regarded it as an honor for the family.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，澣與同職徐台符俱陷塞北。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, Huan and his colleague Xu Taifu both fell captive in the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Bian, Huan and his colleague Xu Taifu both fell captive north of the border.

sentences.zh: 永康王兀欲襲位，置澣宣政殿學士。

translations.literal: When Prince Yongkang Wuyu seized the throne, he appointed Huan Academician of the Xuanzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yongkang Wuyu seized the throne, he appointed Huan Academician of the Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 兀欲死，述律立，以其妻族蕭海貞為幽州節度使。

translations.literal: When Wuyu died, Shulü succeeded to the throne and appointed his wife's clansman Xiao Haizhen military commissioner of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuyu died, Shulü succeeded to the throne and appointed her clansman by marriage, Xiao Haizhen, military commissioner of You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 海貞與澣相善，澣乘間諷海貞以南歸之計，海貞納之。

translations.literal: Haizhen was on good terms with Huan; Huan seized an opportunity to hint to Haizhen a plan to return south, and Haizhen accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Haizhen was on good terms with Huan; Huan seized an opportunity to hint to Haizhen a plan to return south, and Haizhen accepted it.

sentences.zh: 周廣順二年，澣因定州孫方諫密表言契丹衰微之勢，周祖嘉焉，遣諜者田重霸齎詔慰撫，仍命澣通信。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangshun in Zhou, Huan had Sun Fangjian of Ding Prefecture submit a secret memorial on the Khitan's weakening; the Zhou founder was pleased, sent the spy Tian Chongba bearing an edict of comfort and reassurance, and ordered Huan to carry correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangshun in Zhou, Huan had Sun Fangjian of Ding Prefecture submit a secret memorial on the Khitan's weakening. The Zhou founder was pleased, sent the spy Tian Chongba bearing an edict of comfort and reassurance, and ordered Huan to carry correspondence.

sentences.zh: 澣復表述契丹主幼弱多寵，好擊鞠，大臣離貳，若出師討伐，因與通好，乃其時也，請速行之。

translations.literal: Huan again memorialized that the Khitan ruler was young and weak, much indulged by favorites, fond of cuju ball games, and that high ministers were divided—if troops were sent on campaign and friendship was opened at the same time, the time would be right; he asked that this be carried out quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Huan again memorialized that the Khitan ruler was young and weak, much indulged by favorites, fond of cuju, and that the high ministers were divided—if an army were sent on campaign while friendship was opened at the same time, the moment would be right, and he asked that this be done at once.

sentences.zh: 屬中原多事，不能用其言。

translations.literal: But the Central Plains were troubled with many affairs, and his counsel could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: But the Central Plains were beset with many troubles, and his counsel could not be adopted.

sentences.zh: 澣在契丹嘗逃歸，為其所獲，防禦彌謹。

translations.literal: While in Khitan lands Huan once tried to escape and return but was caught; thereafter guards were tightened.
translations.idiomatic: While in Khitan lands Huan once tried to escape south but was captured; thereafter his guard was tightened.

sentences.zh: 契丹應曆十二年六月卒，時建隆三年也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year of Yingli in Khitan he died—at the time it was the third year of Jianlong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twelfth year of Yingli under the Khitan he died—at the time it was the third year of Jianlong.

sentences.zh: 濤收澣文章編之為《丁年集》。

translations.literal: Tao collected Huan's writings and compiled them as the Dingnian Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Tao collected Huan's writings and compiled them as the Dingnian Collection.

sentences.zh: 澣二子，承確，主客郎中，承續，職方郎中。

translations.literal: Huan had two sons: Chengque, Director in the Bureau of Hosts, and Chengxu, Director in the Bureau of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had two sons: Chengque, Director in the Bureau of Hosts, and Chengxu, Director in the Bureau of Works.

sentences.zh: 孫 仲容

translations.literal: Grandson Zhongrong
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Zhongrong

sentences.zh: 仲容，字儀父，舉進士甲科，除大理評事、知三原縣。

translations.literal: Zhongrong, courtesy name Yifu, passed the jinshi in the top class, was appointed Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Sanyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong, whose courtesy name was Yifu, passed the jinshi examination in the top class and was appointed Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Sanyuan County.

sentences.zh: 累擢監察御史，為殿試進士考官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Investigating Censor and served as examiner for the palace jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Investigating Censor and served as examiner for the palace jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 真宗問題義，對稱旨，詔試中書，擢左司諫、直史館。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong questioned him on the meaning of the Classics; his answers pleased the emperor, who ordered a trial at the Secretariat and promoted him to Left Remonstrance and Attendant of the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong questioned him on the meaning of the Classics; his answers pleased the emperor, who ordered a trial at the Secretariat and promoted him to Left Remonstrance and Attendant of the History Office.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，以起居郎為知制誥，累遷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era he served as Drafting Secretary on Attendance and drafter of edicts, and was repeatedly promoted to Right Remonstrance and Advice.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiansheng era he served as Drafting Secretary on Attendance and drafter of edicts, and was repeatedly promoted to Right Remonstrance and Advice.

sentences.zh: 在西掖八年，次當補學士，而不為宰相張士遜所喜，罷為給事中、集賢院學士、判史館、司農寺，復知制誥。

translations.literal: For eight years in the western secretariat his turn to be supplemented as Academician came, but he was not favored by the chancellor Zhang Shisun; he was dismissed to Palace Recipient, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, concurrently Director of the History Office and Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue, and again drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years in the western secretariat his turn to be supplemented as Academician came, but he was not favored by the chancellor Zhang Shisun; he was dismissed to Palace Recipient, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, concurrently Director of the History Office and Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue, and again drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 及石中立、張觀補學士，始以為翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Only when Shi Zhongli and Zhang Guan were supplemented as Academicians was he made Hanlin Attendant Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Shi Zhongli and Zhang Guan were supplemented as Academicians was he made Hanlin Attendant Academician.

sentences.zh: 久之，兼龍圖閣學士，至戶部侍郎卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he was concurrently Academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and died at Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was concurrently Academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and died while serving as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 仲容性醇易，喜飲酒，不與物忤，與人言，未嘗及勢利。

translations.literal: Zhongrong's nature was simple and easygoing; he loved wine, gave no offense, and in conversation never touched on power or profit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong was plain and easygoing by nature. He loved wine, gave offense to no one, and in conversation never touched on power or profit.

sentences.zh: 三弟早卒，字其諸孤十餘人如己子，當世稱其長者。

translations.literal: Three younger brothers died early; he nurtured their orphaned children—more than ten—as if they were his own sons; contemporaries called him a man of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Three younger brothers died early; he raised their orphaned children—more than ten of them—as if they were his own sons, and contemporaries called him a man of virtue.

sentences.zh: 然於吏事非所長。

translations.literal: Yet he was not strong in administrative matters.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was not strong in administrative matters.

sentences.zh: 自集制草為《冠鳳集》十二卷。

translations.literal: He compiled his collected drafts into the Crowned Phoenix Collection in twelve volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled his collected drafts into the Crowned Phoenix Collection in twelve volumes.

sentences.zh: 王易簡

translations.literal: Wang Yijian
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yijian

sentences.zh: 王易簡，字國寶，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wang Yijian, courtesy name Guobao, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yijian, whose courtesy name was Guobao, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 性介特寡合。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright, exceptional, and seldom found company.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and exceptional, and he seldom found company.

sentences.zh: 曾祖朏，唐劍州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Fei was prefect of Jian in Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Fei was prefect of Jian in Tang.

sentences.zh: 祖遠，連州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuan was prefect of Lian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuan was prefect of Lian.

sentences.zh: 父貫，唐州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Guan was prefect of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guan was prefect of Tang.

sentences.zh: 易簡少好學，工詩。

translations.literal: Yijian from youth loved learning and was skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yijian loved learning and was skilled at poetry.

sentences.zh: 會僖宗幸蜀，長安兵亂，避地山谷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong went to Shu, Chang'an was in military chaos, and he fled to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong went to Shu, Chang'an fell into military chaos, and he fled to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 梁乾化中，邵王友誨鎮陝，易簡舉進士，詣府拔解，友誨贈錢二十萬。

translations.literal: In the Ganning era of Liang, when Prince of Shao Youhui governed Shaan, Yijian passed the jinshi examination, went to the prefecture for release from provincial qualification, and Youhui gave him two hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ganning era of Liang, when the Prince of Shao, Youhui, governed Shaan, Yijian passed the jinshi examination, went to the prefecture for release from provincial qualification, and Youhui gave him two hundred thousand in cash.

sentences.zh: 明年遂擢第，復隱華山。

translations.literal: The next year he passed the highest examination and again went into seclusion on Mount Hua.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he passed the highest examination and again withdrew into seclusion on Mount Hua.

sentences.zh: 邠帥韓恭辟觀察支使。

translations.literal: The Binzhou military commissioner Han Gong summoned him as administrative aide of the observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: The Binzhou military commissioner Han Gong summoned him as administrative aide of the observation commission.

sentences.zh: 府罷，華帥李保衡復辟從事。

translations.literal: When the prefecture was abolished, the Hua military commissioner Li Baoheng again summoned him as aide.
translations.idiomatic: When that prefecture was abolished, the Hua military commissioner Li Baoheng again summoned him as aide.

sentences.zh: 逾年，尹皓代保衡，易簡仍在幕府。

translations.literal: More than a year later Yin Hao replaced Baoheng, and Yijian remained in the staff.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Yin Hao replaced Baoheng, and Yijian remained on the staff.

sentences.zh: 會朱友謙以河中叛歸莊宗，攻華州甚急，城中危懼，咸請築月城以自固。

translations.literal: When Zhu Youqian rebelled from Hezhong and submitted to Zhuangzong, he attacked Hua Prefecture fiercely; within the city all were terrified and pleaded to build a crescent bastion for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Youqian rebelled from Hezhong and submitted to Zhuangzong, he pressed the attack on Hua Prefecture fiercely; inside the city all were terrified and pleaded to build a crescent bastion for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 皓恃勇不聽，下令曰：“有敢復言者斬。”

translations.literal: Hao relied on his courage and would not listen; he ordered: "Whoever dares speak of this again shall be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Hao, trusting in his courage, would not listen and ordered, "Whoever dares speak of this again shall be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 易簡固請，乃許。

translations.literal: Yijian pressed his request firmly, and Hao then consented.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian pressed his request firmly, and Hao then consented.

sentences.zh: 板築始畢，外城果壞，軍民賴之。

translations.literal: The rammed-earth walls were just finished when the outer wall indeed collapsed; soldiers and civilians relied on them.
translations.idiomatic: The rammed-earth walls had just been finished when the outer wall indeed collapsed; soldiers and civilians relied on them for their lives.

sentences.zh: 會夜不能攻，友謙遂遁去。

translations.literal: The enemy could not attack through the night, and Youqian then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy could not press the attack through the night, and Youqian then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 皓卒，易簡歸田里。

translations.literal: When Hao died Yijian returned to his village.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao died, Yijian returned to his village.

sentences.zh: 久之，召為著作郎，數月棄去。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned as Editor, but after several months he abandoned the post.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was summoned as Editor, but after several months he abandoned the post.

sentences.zh: 復召為右拾遺，上書忤旨，出為鄧州節度推官。

translations.literal: He was again summoned as Remonstrance and Review on the Right; he submitted a memorial against the emperor's wishes and was sent out as judicial investigator of the Dengzhou military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was again summoned as Remonstrance and Review on the Right; he submitted a memorial against the emperor's wishes and was sent out as judicial investigator under the Dengzhou military commission.

sentences.zh: 晉初，賜金紫，判弘文館、史館事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin he was granted gold and purple, and concurrently directed the Hongwen Academy and History Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Later Jin he was granted gold and purple insignia and concurrently directed the Hongwen Academy and History Office.

sentences.zh: 晉祖為治務求速效，易簡上《漸治論》以諫之，詔書褒答，以論付史館。

translations.literal: The Jin founder in governing sought quick results; Yijian submitted the Gradual Governance Discourse to remonstrate; an edict praised and answered him, and the discourse was sent to the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder in governing sought quick results; Yijian submitted the Gradual Governance Discourse to remonstrate with him. An edict praised and answered him, and the discourse was sent to the History Office.

sentences.zh: 及廢翰林學士，易簡兼知內制，又拜御史中丞，歷右丞、吏部侍郎、左丞、判吏部銓。

translations.literal: When the Hanlin Academicians were abolished, Yijian concurrently managed inner edicts, was again appointed Censor-in-Chief, and successively served as Vice Director on the Right, Vice Minister of Personnel, Vice Director on the Left, and concurrently Director of Personnel Selection.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hanlin Academicians were abolished, Yijian concurrently managed inner edicts, was again appointed Censor-in-Chief, and successively served as Vice Director on the Right, Vice Minister of Personnel, Vice Director on the Left, and concurrently Director of Personnel Selection.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言：“選門格敕條件具存，藩府官僚習熟者少，凡給文解，未曉規程，以致選人詣都，親求解樣，往來跋涉，重可傷閔，傳寫少差，旋復驗放。

translations.literal: He once submitted a memorial: "The regulations and edicts of the selection gate remain fully in force, yet military governors' staff officials are little acquainted with them; whenever they issue examination credentials, they do not understand the rules, so that candidates who reach the capital personally request sample forms, toiling back and forth—a heavy cause for pity—and if copying errs even slightly, they are immediately rejected upon verification.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a memorial: "The regulations and edicts governing the selection gate remain fully in force, yet officials on military governors' staffs are little acquainted with them. Whenever they issue examination credentials, they do not understand the rules, so that candidates who reach the capital must personally request sample forms, toiling back and forth—a grievous waste—and if a copy errs even slightly, it is immediately rejected upon verification.

sentences.zh: 乞自今委南曹詳定解樣，兼錄長定格取解條，下諸州，板置州院門，每取解時，準條式遵行。”

translations.literal: I beg that from now on the Southern Bureau be charged to determine the credential form in detail, and also record the permanent regulations on presenting credentials; send these down to all prefectures, post them on boards at the prefectural yamen gates, and whenever credentials are presented, follow the regulations and forms in compliance."
translations.idiomatic: He requested that from then on the Southern Bureau be charged to set the credential form in detail and to compile the standing rules for presenting credentials; that these be sent to every prefecture and posted on boards at the yamen gates; and that whenever credentials were submitted, the regulations be followed exactly.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 晉祖在大梁，臺省湫隘，易簡奏舉故事，一歲得元省錢二百萬，繕治省署及造器物，號為舉職。

translations.literal: The Jin founder was at Daliang; the central offices were cramped. Yijian memorialized citing precedent and in one year obtained two million strings of original provincial funds, repairing the ministry offices and making furnishings—called fulfilling one's duties.
translations.idiomatic: While the Jin founder held court at Daliang, the central ministries were severely cramped. Yijian memorialized citing precedent and in a single year raised two million strings in original provincial funds, which he used to repair the ministry compounds and supply furnishings—a performance hailed as true fulfillment of office.

sentences.zh: 周朝諱“簡”，易止名易。

translations.literal: The Zhou dynasty tabooed the character "Jian"; Yi shortened his name to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Zhou dynasty tabooed the character for "jian," he shortened his name to Yi alone.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guangshun he was promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 是冬，合三銓為一，令易簡權判，俄改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: That winter the three selection bureaus were merged into one; Yijian was ordered to serve as acting director, and soon after was changed to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the three personnel selection bureaus were merged into one, and Yijian was appointed acting director; shortly afterward he was transferred to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 周祖將親郊，命判兵部，會冊四廟，命為副使。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder was about to perform the imperial suburban sacrifice in person, he was ordered to act as director of the Ministry of War; when the Four Ancestral Temples were enshrined, he was appointed deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder was preparing to conduct the suburban sacrifice in person, Yijian was placed in charge of the Ministry of War; during the enshrinement rites for the Four Ancestral Temples, he served as deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 周祖晏駕，為山陵副使。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder died, he served as deputy commissioner for the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder died, he served as deputy commissioner for the imperial mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年，告老，以太子少保致仕，歸鄉里。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande he requested retirement on grounds of age, retired as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiande 4 he petitioned to retire on grounds of age, stepped down as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 宋初，召加少傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was summoned and given the additional title Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was recalled and further honored as Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 所居華陰，構一鳴堂、二品樓，優遊自適。

translations.literal: He lived at Huayin, built a Hall of Singing Once and a Tower of Second Rank, and lived at ease in contentment.
translations.idiomatic: He made his home in Huayin, where he built the Hall of Singing Once and the Tower of Second Rank, and passed his days in leisurely contentment.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年四月，無疾卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Jianlong he died without illness, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Jianlong 4 he died suddenly, without prior illness, at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 子景讓，進士及第，至尚書郎。

translations.literal: His son Jingrang passed the jinshi examination and rose to a Secretariat director.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingrang passed the jinshi examination and rose to become a director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 趙上交

translations.literal: Zhao Shangjiao
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shangjiao

sentences.zh: 趙上交，涿州范陽人。

translations.literal: Zhao Shangjiao was a native of Fanyang in Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shangjiao came from Fanyang in Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本名遠，字上交，避漢祖諱，遂以字稱。

translations.literal: His original name was Yuan, courtesy name Shangjiao; to avoid the Han founder's taboo he was thereafter known by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yuan and his courtesy name Shangjiao; to avoid the taboo on the Han founder's name, he was known thereafter by his courtesy name alone.

sentences.zh: 祖光鄴，鄂州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guangye was a recording secretary in E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guangye served as recording secretary in E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父簡章，涿州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Jianzhang was Vice Prefect of Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jianzhang served as vice prefect of Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上交身長七尺，黑色，美風儀，善談論，負才任氣，為鄉里所推。

translations.literal: Shangjiao was seven chi tall, dark in complexion, with fine bearing, skilled in discourse, confident in talent and self-willed in spirit, and was esteemed by his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjiao stood seven chi tall, with a dark complexion and handsome bearing. Eloquent and bold, trusting in his own talent and proud in spirit, he was highly regarded in his home district.

sentences.zh: 後唐同光中，嘗詣中山干王都。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era of Later Tang he once went to Zhongshan to seek audience with Wang Du.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang reign of Later Tang he once traveled to Zhongshan to seek an audience with Wang Du.

sentences.zh: 有和少微者亦在都門下，忌之，頗毀訾上交，都遂不為禮。

translations.literal: One He Shaowei was also in Du's service; jealous of Shangjiao, he greatly slandered him, and Du then showed him no courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: A man named He Shaowei also served under Wang Du. Jealous of Shangjiao, he slandered him relentlessly, and Wang Du therefore refused to receive him properly.

sentences.zh: 上交不得志，因南遊洛陽，與中官驃騎大將軍馬紹宏善。

translations.literal: Shangjiao did not achieve his ambition and therefore traveled south to Luoyang, becoming friendly with the eunuch General of Fast Cavalry Ma Shaohong.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to find a patron, Shangjiao went south to Luoyang, where he struck up a friendship with the eunuch general Ma Shaohong.

sentences.zh: 紹宏領北面轉運制置大使，表為判官，遷殿中丞。

translations.literal: Shaohong headed the northern transport commissionerate; he recommended Shangjiao as judicial investigator, and he was promoted to Palace Aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaohong became commissioner for northern transport, he recommended Shangjiao as his judicial investigator, and Shangjiao was promoted to palace aide.

sentences.zh: 秦王從榮開府兼判軍衛，以上交為虞部員外郎，充六軍諸衛推官。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Congrong, opened a princely establishment and concurrently directed the army guard; Shangjiao was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and served as investigating officer for the Six Armies and various guards.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin, Congrong, established his princely establishment and concurrently directed the army guard, Shangjiao was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Works and served as investigating officer for the Six Armies and the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 李澣、張沆、魚崇遠皆白衣在秦府，悉與上交友善。

translations.literal: Li Huan, Zhang Hang, and Yu Chongyuan were all commoners in the Qin princely establishment and all became good friends with Shangjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan, Zhang Hang, and Yu Chongyuan, though still commoners in the prince's household, all became close friends of Shangjiao.

sentences.zh: 累遷司封郎中，充判官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel and served as judicial investigator.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to director in the Ministry of Personnel and served as the prince's judicial investigator.

sentences.zh: 從榮素豪邁，不遵禮法，好昵群小。

translations.literal: Congrong had always been bold and unrestrained, did not observe ritual and law, and liked to draw close to petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong had always been bold and unrestrained, careless of ritual and law, and fond of surrounding himself with petty companions.

sentences.zh: 上交從容言曰：“王位尊崇，當修令德以慰民望，王忍為此，獨不見恭世子、戾太子之事乎？”

translations.literal: Shangjiao spoke calmly and said, "Your princely rank is exalted; you ought to cultivate fine virtue to satisfy the people's hopes. How can Your Highness bear to act thus? Have you alone not seen what befell Crown Prince Gong and Crown Prince Li?"
translations.idiomatic: Shangjiao spoke to him calmly: "Your rank is exalted; you ought to cultivate virtuous conduct to satisfy the people's hopes. How can you bear to act like this? Have you forgotten what happened to Crown Prince Gong and Crown Prince Li?"

sentences.zh: 從榮怒出之，歷涇、秦二鎮州節度判官。

translations.literal: Congrong angrily dismissed him; he successively served as judicial investigator under the military commissioners of Jing and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong angrily dismissed him. Shangjiao then served in turn as judicial investigator under the military commissioners of Jing and Qin.

sentences.zh: 從榮及禍，僚屬皆坐斥，上交由是知名。

translations.literal: When Congrong met calamity, all his staff were punished and dismissed; Shangjiao thereby became famous.
translations.idiomatic: When Congrong's rebellion brought him to ruin, all his staff were punished and dismissed—an outcome that made Shangjiao's name widely known.

sentences.zh: 晉初，召為左司郎中、度支判官，歷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin he was summoned as Director in the Left Office and judicial investigator for revenue, and successively served as Remonstrance and Review on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Later Jin he was recalled as director in the Left Office and revenue investigator, and later served as remonstrance and review on the right.

sentences.zh: 會廢翰林學士，以上交為中書舍人、知內外制，遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Hanlin Academicians were abolished, Shangjiao was made Drafting Archivist and director of inner and outer edicts, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hanlin Academy was abolished, Shangjiao was appointed drafting archivist and put in charge of inner and outer edicts, then promoted to vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言：“伏睹長興中詔書：‘州縣官在任詳讞刑獄、昭雪人命者，不限歲月赴選，許令超資注官，仍賜章服。

translations.literal: He once submitted a memorial: "I have seen the Changxing-era edict: 'If a prefecture or county official, while in office, thoroughly reviews criminal cases and clears wrongfully sentenced persons, regardless of the time of appointment he may proceed to selection and be granted promotion beyond seniority, with an award of insignia.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a memorial: "I have read the Changxing-era edict: 'When a prefecture or county official, while in office, thoroughly reviews criminal cases and vindicates the wrongfully condemned, he may proceed to selection without waiting for the normal term, be granted promotion beyond seniority, and receive an award of insignia.

sentences.zh: 諸道州府給付公驗，躬赴行部投狀，隨給優牒，庶絕欺罔，以存激勸。

translations.literal: Each circuit prefecture and commission shall issue an official certificate; the official shall personally go to the inspectorate and submit a petition, and a commendation document shall be issued forthwith, so that fraud may be eliminated and encouragement preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit, prefecture, and commission shall issue an official certificate; the official shall go in person to the inspectorate and file a petition, whereupon a commendation certificate shall be issued at once—so that fraud may be prevented and merit duly rewarded.

sentences.zh: ’載詳元詔，止言州縣，未該內外職司。

translations.literal: ' On examining the original edict, it speaks only of prefecture and county officials and does not cover inner and outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: ' On examining the original edict, it applies only to prefecture and county officials and does not extend to offices at court or in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 乞自今但能雪活冤獄，不限中外官，並加旌賞。

translations.literal: I beg that from now on, whoever can vindicate the innocent and save lives in unjust cases, whether inner or outer officials, shall all receive commendation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: I request that henceforth any official, whether at court or in the provinces, who vindicates the innocent and saves lives in wrongful cases shall receive commendation and reward.

sentences.zh: 諸道州縣委長吏抄案以聞。

translations.literal: Each circuit, prefecture, and county shall charge the chief official to copy the case and report it.
translations.idiomatic: Let each circuit, prefecture, and county charge its chief official to copy the relevant case and report it upward.

sentences.zh: 俟本人考滿，即詣刑部投狀，毋得隔越年歲，庶使內外同律。”

translations.literal: When the official's term of appraisal is complete, let him go at once to the Ministry of Justice and submit his petition, without allowing years to pass in violation—so that inner and outer offices may be governed by the same rule."
translations.idiomatic: When the official completes his term of service, let him proceed directly to the Ministry of Justice to file his petition, without skipping years in between, so that the same standard may apply at court and in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request by edict.

sentences.zh: 俄遷戶部侍郎，拜御史中丞，彈舉無所阿避。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, appointed Censor-in-Chief, and in impeachments showed favoritism toward none.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was promoted to vice minister of revenue and appointed censor-in-chief; in his impeachments he showed favor to none and shrank from none.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，立明宗幼子許王從益為帝，以禮部尚書王崧為左丞相，上交為右丞相。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, they enthroned Mingzong's young son, Prince Xu Congyi, as emperor, making Wang Song Minister of Rites left chief minister and Shangjiao right chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Bian, they enthroned Mingzong's young son, Prince Xu Congyi, as emperor, appointing Wang Song, minister of rites, as left chief minister and Shangjiao as right chief minister.

sentences.zh: 契丹去，上交請去偽號，稱梁王。

translations.literal: When the Khitan departed, Shangjiao requested removal of the false title and that he be styled Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Khitan withdrew, Shangjiao petitioned to abolish the usurped imperial title and have Congyi styled Prince of Liang instead.

sentences.zh: 漢祖將至，從益遣上交馳表獻款，授檢校禮部尚書、太僕卿，遷秘書監。

translations.literal: When the Han founder was about to arrive, Congyi sent Shangjiao with a fast dispatch presenting allegiance; he was appointed Honorary Minister of Rites and Grand Stable Master, then transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: As the Han founder approached, Congyi sent Shangjiao ahead with a pledge of allegiance; Shangjiao was appointed honorary minister of rites and grand stable master, then promoted to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 周祖監國，命太師馮道迎湘陰公於徐州，以上交副之。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder supervised the state, he ordered Grand Preceptor Feng Dao to welcome the Duke of Xiangyin at Xuzhou, with Shangjiao as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder assumed supervisory rule, he ordered Grand Preceptor Feng Dao to welcome the Duke of Xiangyin at Xuzhou, with Shangjiao as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 會將試貢士，上交申明條制，頗為精密，始復糊名考校。

translations.literal: When the examination of tribute scholars was about to be held, Shangjiao clarified the regulations with considerable precision, and the sealed-name examination was restored for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: When the civil service examination was about to be held, Shangjiao set out the regulations with unusual precision, restoring for the first time the practice of sealed-name grading.

sentences.zh: 擢扈載甲科，及取梁周翰、董淳之流，時稱得士。

translations.literal: He selected Hu Zai in the top grade and also took men such as Liang Zhouhan and Dong Chun; at the time he was said to have obtained true talent.
translations.idiomatic: He placed Hu Zai in the top grade and also selected men such as Liang Zhouhan and Dong Chun; contemporaries praised him for having chosen genuine talent.

sentences.zh: 轉戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年再知舉，謗議紛然。

translations.literal: The next year he again directed the examination, and slander and criticism arose on every side.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when he directed the examination again, criticism erupted on all sides.

sentences.zh: 時樞密使王峻用事，常薦童子，上交拒之。

translations.literal: At the time Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Jun was in power and often recommended young students; Shangjiao refused.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the military affairs commissioner Wang Jun held real power and often pressed recommendations of favored candidates; Shangjiao refused them.

sentences.zh: 峻怒，奏上交選士失實，貶商州司馬，朝議以為太重，會峻貶乃止，但坐所取士李觀、侯璨賦落韻，改太子詹事。

translations.literal: Jun grew angry and memorialized that Shangjiao's selection of scholars was false; he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Shangzhou. Court opinion held the punishment too severe, but when Jun himself was demoted the matter stopped—yet because the scholars he had selected, Li Guan and Hou Can, had rhyme errors in their rhapsodies, Shangjiao was instead punished by appointment as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Jun grew furious and memorialized that Shangjiao had falsified the selection of scholars, and Shangjiao was demoted to vice prefect of Shangzhou. Court opinion held the punishment excessive, but when Jun himself was demoted the demotion was halted—though because the candidates Shangjiao had passed, Li Guan and Hou Can, had committed rhyme violations in their rhapsodies, he was instead stripped of his post and made grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，遷賓客。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was transferred to Host for Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiande he was transferred to host for the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜吏部侍郎，多請告不朝，時出遊別墅。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel; he often requested leave and did not attend court, going out at times to his villa.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed vice minister of personnel; he frequently took leave from court and was often found at his country villa.

sentences.zh: 世宗因問陶穀曰：“上交豈衰老乎？”

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong thereupon asked Tao Gu, "Has Shangjiao grown old and feeble?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong then asked Tao Gu, "Has Shangjiao simply grown old?"

sentences.zh: 穀對曰：“上交昔掌貢舉，放鬻市家子李觀及第，受所獻名園，多植花卉，優遊自適。”

translations.literal: Gu replied, "When Shangjiao formerly directed the examination, he passed Li Guan, the son of a market vendor, received from him a famed garden as a gift, planted many flowers, and lived at ease in contentment."
translations.idiomatic: Tao Gu replied, "When Shangjiao directed the examinations, he passed Li Guan—the son of a market vendor—accepted a famous garden Li offered him, filled it with flowers, and lived there in leisurely comfort."

sentences.zh: 世宗怒，免其官。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and stripped him of his office.

sentences.zh: 宋初，起為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was raised up as Vice Director of the Secretariat on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was recalled as vice director of the secretariat on the right.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年正月，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Jianlong he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jianlong 2 he died at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 上交所蒞官以幹聞，當時稱有公輔器。

translations.literal: Shangjiao was known for competence in office and was at the time said to possess the makings of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjiao was known for executive ability in office, and contemporaries said he had the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 尤好吟詠，有集二十卷，張昭為序。

translations.literal: He especially loved composing poetry; he had a collection in twenty scrolls, for which Zhang Zhao wrote the preface.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially fond of poetry; his collected works ran to twenty scrolls, with a preface by Zhang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 子曮，字可畏。

translations.literal: His son Yan, courtesy name Kewei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan, whose courtesy name was Kewei.

sentences.zh: 七歲喪母過哀。

translations.literal: At age seven he lost his mother and grieved excessively.
translations.idiomatic: When he was seven he lost his mother and mourned with exceptional grief.

sentences.zh: 十二能屬文，與兄晙同舉進士，未成名而兄夭，遂以蔭補千牛備身，歷秘書郎、殿中丞、著作郎。

translations.literal: At twelve he could compose literary pieces; he and his elder brother Jun both took the jinshi examination; before achieving fame his brother died young, and he therefore entered office by yin privilege as an armed attendant of the heir apparent, successively serving as Secretariat attendant, Palace Aide, and Editor.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he could already write competently. He and his elder brother Jun both attempted the jinshi examination; before either could make a name, his brother died young, and Yan entered office by yin privilege as an armed attendant of the heir apparent, later serving as secretariat attendant, palace aide, and editor.

sentences.zh: 卒，年二十六。

translations.literal: He died, aged twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷，太宗嘗取以入內。

translations.literal: He had a collection in ten scrolls; Emperor Taizong once had it brought into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection of ten scrolls, which Emperor Taizong once had brought into the palace.

sentences.zh: 張錫，福州閩縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xi was a native of Min County in Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xi came from Min County in Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 梁末，劉君鐸任棣州刺史，辟為軍事判官。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang, Liu Junduo served as prefect of Di Prefecture and summoned him as military judicial investigator.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Liang, when Liu Junduo became prefect of Di, he recruited Xi as his military judicial investigator.

sentences.zh: 棣為鄆之屬郡，郡有麴務，鄆以牙將主之，頗橫恣，民有犯麴三斤，牙將欲置於死，君鐸力不能救。

translations.literal: Di was a subordinate prefecture of Yun; the prefecture had a liquor monopoly office, which Yun placed under a guard officer who was quite overbearing and lawless. When a commoner violated the liquor law by three jin, the guard officer wished to put him to death, and Junduo could not save him by force.
translations.idiomatic: Di was subordinate to Yun Prefecture, which maintained a liquor monopoly administered by a guard officer who ruled with gross arrogance. When a man was found with three jin of illicit liquor, the guard officer sought to execute him, and Junduo was powerless to intervene.

sentences.zh: 既而牙將盜麥百斛私造麴，事覺，錫判曰：“麴犯三斤，求生不克，麥盜百斛，免死誠難。”

translations.literal: Soon after, the guard officer stole a hundred hu of wheat and privately brewed liquor; when the matter was discovered, Xi rendered judgment: "For a liquor offense of three jin one could not obtain life; for stealing a hundred hu of wheat, exemption from death is truly difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward the guard officer stole a hundred hu of wheat and brewed liquor on his own; when the crime came to light, Xi rendered judgment: "A man guilty of three jin of illicit liquor could not obtain mercy—yet one who steals a hundred hu of wheat can hardly expect to escape death."

sentences.zh: 時郡吏以使府牙將乞免，錫不允，固置於法。

translations.literal: At the time the prefectural clerks, acting for the military commission's guard officer, begged exemption; Xi did not consent and firmly had him executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural clerks, acting on behalf of the guard officer from the military commission, pleaded for leniency, but Xi refused and had the man executed according to law.

sentences.zh: 同光末，趙在禮舉兵於鄴，瀕河諸州多構亂，錫權知州事，即出省錢賞軍，皆大悅，一郡獨全，棣人賴之。

translations.literal: At the end of Tongguang, Zhao Zaili raised troops at Ye; prefectures along the Yellow River mostly fell into disorder. Xi acted as provisional prefect and immediately disbursed provincial funds to reward the army; all were greatly pleased, and the prefecture alone remained intact—the people of Di relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tongguang, when Zhao Zaili rebelled at Ye, prefectures along the Yellow River fell into turmoil one after another. Xi acted as provisional prefect and immediately paid out provincial funds to reward the troops; the soldiers were delighted, and Di alone remained secure—its people owed their safety to him.

sentences.zh: 後為淄川令，不畏強禦，專務愛民，刺史有所徵，不答，由是銜之。

translations.literal: Later he served as magistrate of Zichuan, feared no strong oppression, and devoted himself to caring for the people. When the prefect sought levies from him he did not respond, and for this the prefect harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as magistrate of Zichuan, he feared no powerful bully and devoted himself wholly to the people's welfare. When the prefect demanded levies he refused to comply, and the prefect thereafter bore him a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及代，白其事於宰相馮道。

translations.literal: When his term ended, he reported the matter to Chief Minister Feng Dao.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, he reported the affair to Chief Minister Feng Dao.

sentences.zh: 道知錫介直，即奏召為監察御史，出為陝、虢觀察判官。

translations.literal: Dao knew Xi's integrity and forthrightness and at once memorialized to summon him as Investigating Censor; he went out as judicial investigator under the Shan and Guo observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing Xi's upright character, Dao immediately memorialized to have him summoned as investigating censor; Xi was then sent out as judicial investigator under the Shan-Guo observation commission.

sentences.zh: 晉開運二年，拜右補闕，歷起居郎、刑部員外郎、開封府判官、浚儀令、司門駕部二郎中，並以清節聞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun of Jin he was appointed Supplementer on the Right, successively served as Diarist, Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, judicial investigator of Kaifeng prefecture, magistrate of Junyi, and both Directors in the Ministry of Revenue—always known for incorruptible conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun 2 of Later Jin he was appointed right supplementer and successively served as diarist, vice director in the ministry of justice, judicial investigator of Kaifeng, magistrate of Junyi, and director in the ministries of revenue and works—always renowned for incorruptible conduct.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，以老疾求解官，授右諫議大夫致政。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou, on grounds of age and illness he requested release from office and was granted retirement as Remonstrance and Review on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande reign of Later Zhou, citing age and illness he requested retirement and was granted it with the title remonstrance and review on the right.

sentences.zh: 宋初，改給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was changed to Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was reassigned as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 錫無子，宰相范質嘗兄事之，館於別墅。

translations.literal: Xi had no son; Chief Minister Fan Zhi once treated him as an elder brother and lodged him at his villa.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had no sons; Chief Minister Fan Zhi treated him as an elder brother and kept him at his country estate.

sentences.zh: 錫以執政之門，不欲久處，往依鄉人鄧州觀察判官黃保緒。

translations.literal: Xi, considering it improper to dwell long at the home of a chief minister, went to live with his townsman Huang Baoxu, judicial investigator under the Dengzhou observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to remain long in a chief minister's household, Xi went to stay with his fellow townsman Huang Baoxu, judicial investigator under the Dengzhou observation commission.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年六月，卒於穰下。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Jianlong he died at Rangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Jianlong 2 he died at Rang.

sentences.zh: 張鑄，字司化，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhu, courtesy name Sihua, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhu, whose courtesy name was Sihua, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 性清介，不事生產。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure and upright and did not engage in livelihood pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and austere and took no interest in material gain.

sentences.zh: 曾祖居卿，祖裼，父文蔚，在唐俱舉進士。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Juqing, grandfather Ti, and father Wenwei all passed the jinshi examination under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Juqing, grandfather Ti, and father Wenwei had all passed the jinshi examination under the Tang.

sentences.zh: 裼至翰林學士承旨、天平軍節度、檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Ti rose to Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance, military commissioner of Tianping Army, and Honorary Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Ti rose to Hanlin academician-in-attendance, military commissioner of Tianping, and honorary minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 文蔚，中書侍郎、平章事，《五代史》有傳。

translations.literal: Wenwei served as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor; he has a biography in the History of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei served as vice director of the secretariat and grand councilor; his biography appears in the History of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 鑄，梁貞明三年舉進士，補福昌衛、集賢校理，拜監察御史，遷殿侍御史。

translations.literal: Zhu, in the third year of Zhenming of Liang, passed the jinshi examination, was appointed to the Fuchang Guard and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was appointed Investigating Censor, and was promoted to Palace Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu passed the jinshi examination in Zhenming 3 of Later Liang, was appointed to the Fuchang guard and as collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then became investigating censor and was promoted to palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 仕後唐，歷起居郎、金部員外郎，賜緋，改右司員外郎。

translations.literal: Serving Later Tang, he successively served as Diarist and Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, was granted crimson insignia, and was changed to Vice Director in the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Tang he served successively as diarist and vice director in the ministry of revenue, was granted crimson insignia, and was transferred to vice director in the right office.

sentences.zh: 明宗初，轉金部郎中，賜金紫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingzong he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Mingzong's reign he was promoted to director in the ministry of revenue and granted gold and purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言曰：“國家以務農為本，守令以勸課為先，廣辟田疇，用實倉廩。

translations.literal: He once submitted a memorial: "The state takes devotion to agriculture as its foundation; prefects and magistrates take encouragement of cultivation as their first duty, broadly opening fields to fill the granaries in reality.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a memorial: "The state takes agriculture as its foundation, and prefects and magistrates must make the encouragement of farming their first duty, opening fields broadly so that the granaries may be genuinely filled.

sentences.zh: 竊見所在鄉村浮戶，方事墾辟，甫成生計，種田未至二頃，植木未及十年，縣司以定色役，民畏責斂，捨之而去，殊乖撫恤之方，徒設招攜之令。

translations.literal: I observe that floating households in the villages are just then opening wasteland and have barely established livelihoods; planted fields have not yet reached two qing, planted trees not yet ten years—yet the county office fixes corvée assignments; the people fear tax levies, abandon their holdings, and leave—greatly contrary to the policy of nurturing care, making empty the policy of recruitment and settlement.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed that migrant households in the countryside are just beginning to reclaim wasteland and have barely established a livelihood; their fields amount to less than two qing and their trees are fewer than ten years old—yet county officials already fix their corvée assignments. Fearing tax levies, these people abandon their holdings and flee—precisely the opposite of compassionate governance, and a mockery of policies meant to attract settlers.

sentences.zh: 望令諸州應有荒田縱民墾蒔，俟及五頃已上，三年外始聽差科。”

translations.literal: I hope that an order be issued that in all prefectures abandoned fields shall be opened to the people for reclamation and planting, and that corvée and levies be imposed only after five qing or more have been reached and only after three years have passed."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all prefectures be ordered to allow the people to reclaim and cultivate wasteland freely, and that corvée and tax levies be imposed only after holdings reach five qing and only after three years have elapsed.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 使兩浙還，遷考功郎中。

translations.literal: Returning from a mission to the Two Zhes, he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel for merit evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from a mission to the Two Zhes, he was promoted to director in the ministry of personnel charged with merit evaluation.

sentences.zh: 鑄美姿儀，善筆劄，老能燈下細書如蠅頭。

translations.literal: Zhu had fine appearance and bearing, was skilled at letters, and in old age could write fine script by lamplight like fly heads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was handsome in bearing and skilled with the brush; even in old age he could write by lamplight script as fine as fly's heads.

sentences.zh: 由晉以來，天地、宗廟及上徽號、封拜王公冊文，皆詔鑄書之。

translations.literal: From Jin onward, the documents for Heaven and Earth, ancestral temples, and imperial honorific titles, and the appointment texts for enfeoffing kings and dukes, were all ordered written by Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: From Later Jin onward, he was commissioned to write all sacrificial texts for Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples, all documents conferring imperial honorific titles, and all investiture scrolls for kings and dukes.

sentences.zh: 及卒，身無兼衣，家人鬻其服馬、園圃，得錢十萬以葬。

translations.literal: When he died he had no spare set of clothes; his family sold his clothes, horses, and garden for a hundred thousand cash to bury him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he did not even own a change of clothes; his family sold his garments, horses, and garden for a hundred thousand cash to pay for his burial.

sentences.zh: 邊歸讜

translations.literal: Bian Guidang
translations.idiomatic: Bian Guidang

sentences.zh: 邊歸讜，字安正，幽州薊人，父退思，檀州刺史。

translations.literal: Bian Guidang, courtesy name Anzheng, was a native of Ji in You Prefecture; his father Tuisi was prefect of Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Guidang, whose courtesy name was Anzheng, came from Ji in You Prefecture; his father Tuisi had served as prefect of Tan.

sentences.zh: 歸讜弱冠以儒學名。

translations.literal: Guidang in his youth was famed for Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Guidang was already known for Confucian scholarship while still in his teens.

sentences.zh: 後唐末，客遊幷、邠。

translations.literal: At the end of Later Tang he traveled as a guest in Bing and Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Later Tang he traveled as a guest scholar in Bing and Bin.

sentences.zh: 晉祖鎮太原，召置門下，表為河東節度推官、試秘書省校書郎，改太原府推官、試大理評事。

translations.literal: When the Jin founder was stationed at Taiyuan, he summoned Guichan and placed him in his service; Guichan was recommended as investigating officer of the Hedong military commission, Acting Collator of the Secretariat, then changed to investigating officer of Taiyuan Prefecture and Acting Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Jin founder was stationed at Taiyuan, he summoned Guichan into his service. Guichan was recommended as investigating officer of the Hedong military commission and Acting Collator of the Secretariat, then transferred to investigating officer of Taiyuan Prefecture and Acting Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 天福初，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu he was appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianfu era he was appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 歷殿中侍御史、禮部員外郎，充戶部判官。

translations.literal: He successively served as Palace Attendant Censor and Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, and served as administrative aide in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Palace Attendant Censor and Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, and also served as administrative aide in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 遷水部郎中，賜金紫，拜比部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Works, granted gold and purple, and appointed Director of the Ministry of Revenue and charged with drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Works and granted gold and purple insignia, then appointed Director of the Ministry of Revenue and charged with drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 歷右諫議大夫、給事中。

translations.literal: He successively served as Right Remonstrance Counselor and Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Right Remonstrance Counselor and Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言：“使臣經過州縣，券料外妄自徵需，以豐傔從，多索人驢，用遞行李。

translations.literal: He once submitted a memorial: "When envoys pass through prefectures and counties, beyond their authorized vouchers they recklessly levy demands to enrich their attendants, often requisitioning people's donkeys to transport relay baggage.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a memorial: "When envoys pass through prefectures and counties, beyond their authorized vouchers they recklessly levy demands to enrich their attendants, often requisitioning people's donkeys to transport relay baggage.

sentences.zh: 挾命為勢，淩下作威，供億稍遲，即加鞭箠，吏民受辱，寧免怨嗟。

translations.literal: Wielding their commission as power, they lord it over subordinates and throw their weight around; if provisions are slightly delayed they immediately add whipping and beating—how can officials and commoners who suffer such insults avoid resentment and lament?
translations.idiomatic: Wielding their commissions as power, they lord it over subordinates and throw their weight around. If provisions are even slightly delayed they immediately resort to whipping and beating. How can officials and commoners who suffer such insults avoid resentment and lament?

sentences.zh: 欲望察訪得情，嚴示懲戒。”

translations.literal: I hope that investigation may ascertain the facts and stern punishment be displayed as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: I hope that investigations may ascertain the facts and stern punishment be displayed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 俄遷右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse.

sentences.zh: 漢初，歷禮部、刑部二侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he successively served as Vice Minister of Rites and Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Later Han he successively served as Vice Minister of Rites and Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時史弘肇怙權專殺，閭里告訐成風。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Hongzhao relied on power and killed at will, and denunciation among neighbors became the fashion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shi Hongzhao relied on power and killed at will, and denunciation among neighbors became the fashion.

sentences.zh: 歸讜言曰：“邇來有匿名書及言風聞事，構害善良，有傷風化，遂使貪吏得以報復私怨，讒夫得以肆其虛誕。

translations.literal: Guichan said: "Recently there have been anonymous letters and reports based on hearsay that frame and harm the good, injuring public morals, so that greedy officials can avenge private grudges and slanderers can indulge their fabrications.
translations.idiomatic: Guichan said, "Recently there have been anonymous letters and reports based on hearsay that frame and harm the good, injuring public morals, so that greedy officials can avenge private grudges and slanderers can indulge their fabrications.

sentences.zh: 請明行條制，禁遏誣罔。

translations.literal: I request that regulations be clearly promulgated to forbid and stop false accusations.
translations.idiomatic: I request that regulations be clearly promulgated to forbid and stop false accusations.

sentences.zh: 凡顯有披論，具陳姓名。

translations.literal: Whenever there is an open accusation, the accuser's name should be fully stated.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there is an open accusation, the accuser's name should be fully stated.

sentences.zh: 其匿名書及風聞事者並望止絕。”

translations.literal: Anonymous letters and hearsay reports should all be stopped entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Anonymous letters and hearsay reports should all be stopped entirely.

sentences.zh: 論者韙之。

translations.literal: Commentators approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators approved of this.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，遷兵部、戶部二侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun of Zhou he was transferred to Vice Minister of War and Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangshun era of Later Zhou he was transferred to Vice Minister of War and Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞其亮直，擢為尚書右丞、樞密直學士，以備顧問。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong heard of his integrity and forthrightness and promoted him to Vice Director of the Secretariat on the Right and Academician-in-Attendance of the Privy Council, to serve as an adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong heard of his integrity and forthrightness and promoted him to Vice Director of the Secretariat on the Right and Academician-in-Attendance of the Privy Council, to serve as an adviser.

sentences.zh: 就轉左丞，世宗以累朝以來憲綱不振，命為御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was immediately transferred to Vice Director on the Left; because over successive reigns the censorial regulations had not been enforced, Emperor Shizong appointed him Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately transferred to Vice Director on the Left. Because over successive reigns the censorial regulations had not been enforced, Emperor Shizong appointed him Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 歸讜雖號廉直，而性剛介，言多忤物。

translations.literal: Although Guichan was known as incorrupt and upright, by nature he was rigid and uncompromising, and his words often offended others.
translations.idiomatic: Although Guichan was known as incorrupt and upright, by nature he was rigid and uncompromising, and his words often offended others.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年冬，大宴廣德殿，歸讜酒酣，揚袂言曰：“至於一杯而已。”

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Xiande, at a great banquet in the Hall of Broad Virtue, Guichan, flushed with wine, waved his sleeve and said: "It comes to no more than one cup, that's all."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Xiande, at a great banquet in the Hall of Broad Virtue, Guichan, flushed with wine, waved his sleeve and said, "It comes to no more than one cup, that's all."

sentences.zh: 世宗命黃門扶出之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong ordered the palace attendants to support him out.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong ordered the palace attendants to escort him out.

sentences.zh: 歸讜回顧曰：“陛下何不決殺趙守微。”

translations.literal: Guichan looked back and said: "Your Majesty, why not simply execute Zhao Shouwei?"
translations.idiomatic: Guichan looked back and said, "Your Majesty, why not simply execute Zhao Shouwei?"

sentences.zh: 守微者，本村民，因獻策擢拾遺，有妻復娶，又言涉指斥，坐決杖配流，故歸讜語及之。

translations.literal: Shouwei had originally been a village commoner; because he submitted a policy proposal he was promoted to Reminder, but he took a second wife while his first still lived, and his words were also deemed seditious, for which he was sentenced to beating with the rod and exile—hence Guichan mentioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwei had originally been a village commoner. Because he submitted a policy proposal he was promoted to Reminder, but he took a second wife while his first still lived, and his words were also deemed seditious, for which he was sentenced to beating with the rod and exile—hence Guichan mentioned him.

sentences.zh: 翌日，伏閣請罪，詔釋之，仍於閣門復飲數爵，以愧其心。

translations.literal: The next day he prostrated himself at the palace gate to beg forgiveness; an edict pardoned him, and he was made to drink several more cups at the Gate Pavilion to shame his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he prostrated himself at the palace gate to beg forgiveness. An edict pardoned him, and he was made to drink several more cups at the Gate Pavilion to shame him into repentance.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，歸讜與百官班廣德殿門外，忽厲聲聞於帝，詔奪一季奉。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year, as Guichan stood in rank with the officials outside the gate of the Hall of Broad Virtue, he suddenly raised his voice loudly enough for the emperor to hear; an edict stripped him of one season's salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year, as Guichan stood in rank with the officials outside the gate of the Hall of Broad Virtue, he suddenly raised his voice loudly enough for the emperor to hear. An edict stripped him of one season's salary.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song dynasty he was transferred to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，告老，拜戶部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong he requested retirement on grounds of age and was granted Minister of Revenue in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong he requested retirement on grounds of age and was granted Minister of Revenue in retirement.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande he died, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子定，雍熙二年進士及第。

translations.literal: His son Ding passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ding passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yongxi.

sentences.zh: 劉溫叟

translations.literal: Liu Wensou
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wensou

sentences.zh: 劉溫叟，字永齡，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Wensou, style name Yongling, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wensou, style name Yongling, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 性重厚方正，動遵禮法。

translations.literal: By nature he was grave, solid, and upright, and in his conduct he always observed ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was grave, solid, and upright, and in his conduct he always observed ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 唐武德功臣政會之後。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Zhenghui, a meritorious minister of the Wude era of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He was a descendant of Zhenghui, a meritorious minister of the Wude era of Tang.

sentences.zh: 叔祖崇望，相昭宗。

translations.literal: His grand-uncle Chongwang served as chief minister to Emperor Zhaozong.
translations.idiomatic: His grand-uncle Chongwang served as chief minister to Emperor Zhaozong.

sentences.zh: 父岳，後唐太常卿。

translations.literal: His father Yue was Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices under Later Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yue served as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices under Later Tang.

sentences.zh: 溫叟七歲能屬文，善楷隸。

translations.literal: At seven Wensou could compose prose and was skilled in regular and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seven Wensou could compose prose and was skilled in regular and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 岳時退居洛中，語家人曰：“吾兒風骨秀異，所未知者壽耳。

translations.literal: When Yue was retired and living in Luoyang, he told his family: "My son's bearing and bone structure are outstanding; the only thing unknown is his span of life.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was retired and living in Luoyang, he told his family, "My son's bearing and bone structure are outstanding. The only thing unknown is his span of life.

sentences.zh: 今世難未息，得與老夫皆為溫、洛之叟足矣。”

translations.literal: In this age troubles have not yet ceased; it would be enough if he and I old man could both become old men of Wen and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: In this age troubles have not yet ceased. It would be enough if he and I could both grow old as men of Wen and Luo.

sentences.zh: 故名之溫叟。

translations.literal: Hence he was named Wensou.
translations.idiomatic: Hence he was named Wensou.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補國子四門助教，河南府文學。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Four Gates in the Directorate of Education and Literary Scholar of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: By yin privilege he was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Four Gates in the Directorate of Education and Literary Scholar of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，為左拾遺、內供奉。

translations.literal: During Qingtai he served as Left Reminder and Inner Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingtai era he served as Left Reminder and Inner Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以母老乞歸就養，改監察御史，分司。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he requested to return home to support her, and was changed to Supervising Censor with a detached commission.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was old he requested to return home to support her, and was changed to Supervising Censor with a detached commission.

sentences.zh: 時臺署廢弛，溫叟作新之。

translations.literal: At the time the censorate offices had fallen into neglect, and Wensou restored them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the censorate offices had fallen into neglect, and Wensou restored them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召為右補闕。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Right Supplementation Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to serve as Right Supplementation Secretary.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，溫叟懼，隨契丹北遷，與承旨張允共上表求解職。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, Wensou was afraid and followed the Khitan north; together with Expositor-in-Chief Zhang Yun he submitted a memorial requesting release from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Bian, Wensou was afraid and followed the Khitan north. Together with Expositor-in-Chief Zhang Yun he submitted a memorial requesting release from office.

sentences.zh: 契丹主怒，欲出允等為縣令。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler grew angry and wished to send Yun and the others out as county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler grew angry and wished to send Yun and the others out as county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽曰：“若學士才不稱職求解者，守本官可也，不可加貶出。”

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou said: "If an academician's talent does not fit his post and he requests release, he may keep his original rank—that is enough; he should not be further demoted and sent out."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou said, "If an academician's talent does not fit his post and he requests release, he may keep his original rank—that is enough. He should not be further demoted and sent out."

sentences.zh: 遂得罷職出院。

translations.literal: Thus they were able to resign their posts and leave the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they were able to resign their posts and leave the academy.

sentences.zh: 漢祖南下，溫叟自洛從至鄭州，稱疾不行。

translations.literal: When the Han founder marched south, Wensou followed from Luoyang as far as Zhengzhou, then claimed illness and did not go on.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder marched south, Wensou followed from Luoyang as far as Zhengzhou, then claimed illness and did not go on.

sentences.zh: 及入汴，溫叟久之方至，授駕部郎中。

translations.literal: When he entered Bian, Wensou arrived only after a long delay and was granted Director of the Carriage Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder entered Bian, Wensou arrived only after a long delay and was granted Director of the Carriage Bureau.

sentences.zh: 周初，拜左諫議大夫，逾年，改中書舍人，加史館修撰，判館事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou he was appointed Left Remonstrance Counselor; after a year he was changed to Secretariat Drafter, given the additional title of Compiler of the History Office, and directed its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Later Zhou he was appointed Left Remonstrance Counselor. After a year he was changed to Secretariat Drafter, given the additional title of Compiler of the History Office, and directed its affairs.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，遷禮部侍郎、知貢舉，得進士十六人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and served as chief examiner, selecting sixteen jinshi.
