translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiande era he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and served as chief examiner, selecting sixteen jinshi.

sentences.zh: 有譖於帝者，帝怒，黜十二人，左遷太子詹事。

translations.literal: Someone slandered him to the emperor; the emperor grew angry, dismissed twelve of the candidates, and demoted Wensou to Heir Apparent Household Director.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered him to the emperor. The emperor grew angry, dismissed twelve of the candidates, and demoted Wensou to Heir Apparent Household Director.

sentences.zh: 溫叟實無私，後數年，其被黜者相繼登第。

translations.literal: Wensou had in fact shown no partiality; several years later those who had been dismissed passed the examinations in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wensou had in fact shown no partiality. Several years later those who had been dismissed passed the examinations in succession.

sentences.zh: 溫叟與張昭同修漢隱帝及周祖實錄，恭帝即位，遷工部侍郎兼判國子祭酒事。

translations.literal: Wensou and Zhang Zhao together compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Yindi of Han and the Zhou founder; when Emperor Gongdi ascended the throne, Wensou was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and concurrently directed the affairs of the Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Wensou and Zhang Zhao together compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Yindi of Later Han and the Zhou founder. When Emperor Gongdi ascended the throne, Wensou was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and concurrently directed the affairs of the Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 宋初，改刑部。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was changed to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song dynasty he was transferred to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 建隆九年，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jianlong he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Jianlong he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，退居西洛，旋復本官。

translations.literal: Upon the death of his mother he withdrew to western Luoyang, and soon resumed his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Upon the death of his mother he withdrew to western Luoyang, and soon resumed his original post.

sentences.zh: 三年，兼判吏部銓。

translations.literal: In the third year he concurrently directed the Ministry of Personnel selection board.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he concurrently directed the Ministry of Personnel selection board.

sentences.zh: 因上言曰：“伏見兩京百司，漸乏舊人，多隳故事。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted a memorial, saying: "I respectfully observe that in the hundred offices of the two capitals, veterans are gradually lacking and precedents are often abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted a memorial, saying, "I respectfully observe that in the hundred offices of the two capitals, veterans are gradually lacking and precedents are often abandoned.

sentences.zh: 雖檢閱具存於往冊，而舉行須在於攸司。

translations.literal: Although review shows them fully preserved in former registers, their implementation depends on the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Although review shows them fully preserved in former registers, their implementation depends on the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 蓋因年限得官，歸司者例與減選；

translations.literal: This is because those who obtain office by seniority and return to their bureaus are by precedent given reduced selection credit;
translations.idiomatic: This is because those who obtain office by seniority and return to their bureaus are by precedent given reduced selection credit;

sentences.zh: 冬集赴調，授任者尋又出京。

translations.literal: those who attend the winter assembly for appointment, once given posts, soon leave the capital again.
translations.idiomatic: those who attend the winter assembly for appointment, once given posts, soon leave the capital again.

sentences.zh: 兼有裁滿初官，不還舊局，但稱前資，用圖免役。

translations.literal: There are also those whose initial appointments have expired who do not return to their former bureaus but cite prior qualifications to seek exemption from service.
translations.idiomatic: There are also those whose initial appointments have expired who do not return to their former bureaus but cite prior qualifications to seek exemption from service.

sentences.zh: 又有嘗因停任，切欲歸司，而元敕不該，無由復職。

translations.literal: There are also those who once had their appointments suspended and earnestly wish to return to their bureaus, but the original edict does not cover their cases and they have no way to resume their posts.
translations.idiomatic: There are also those who once had their appointments suspended and earnestly wish to return to their bureaus, but the original edict does not cover their cases and they have no way to resume their posts.

sentences.zh: 遂使在司者失於教習，歷事者難於追還。

translations.literal: Thus those remaining in the bureaus lack instruction and training, and those with experience are hard to recall.
translations.idiomatic: Thus those remaining in the bureaus lack instruction and training, and those with experience are hard to recall.

sentences.zh: 伏望自今諸司職掌，除官勒留及歸司者，如理減外欠三選以下，仍須在司執行公事，及三十月即許赴集；

translations.literal: I respectfully hope that from now on, for all bureau posts, except those ordered to remain or returning to their bureaus, if beyond reasonable reduction they owe fewer than three selections, they must still perform official duties in the bureau, and after thirty months may be permitted to attend the assembly;
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully hope that from now on, for all bureau posts, except those ordered to remain or returning to their bureaus, if beyond reasonable reduction they owe fewer than three selections, they must still perform official duties in the bureau, and after thirty months may be permitted to attend the assembly;

sentences.zh: 如理選外欠三選以上，及在官不成資考者，即準元敕處分。

translations.literal: if beyond reasonable selection credit they owe three selections or more, or if while in office they fail to complete a term of evaluation, they should be handled according to the original edict.
translations.idiomatic: if beyond reasonable selection credit they owe three selections or more, or if while in office they fail to complete a term of evaluation, they should be handled according to the original edict.

sentences.zh: 若在任停官及在司停職者，經恩後於刑部出給雪牒，卻勒歸司，如無闕員，即令守闕，餘依敕格處分。

translations.literal: If while in post one's appointment is suspended or while in the bureau one's duties are suspended, after an amnesty the Ministry of Justice should issue a vindication certificate, and the official should then be ordered back to the bureau; if there is no vacancy, he should be made to await one, and the rest handled according to edicts and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: If while in post one's appointment is suspended or while in the bureau one's duties are suspended, after an amnesty the Ministry of Justice should issue a vindication certificate, and the official should then be ordered back to the bureau. If there is no vacancy, he should be made to await one, and the rest handled according to edicts and regulations.

sentences.zh: 一日晚歸由闕前，太祖方與中黃門數人偶登明德門西闕，前騶者潛知之，以白溫叟。

translations.literal: One day, returning late, he passed before the gate tower; Taizu happened to be ascending the western tower of the Gate of Bright Virtue with several palace attendants. The outriders secretly learned of this and informed Wensou.
translations.idiomatic: One day, returning late, he passed before the gate tower. Taizu happened to be ascending the western tower of the Gate of Bright Virtue with several palace attendants. The outriders secretly learned of this and informed Wensou.

sentences.zh: 溫叟令傳呼如常過闕。

translations.literal: Wensou ordered the heralds to announce his passage as usual when crossing before the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wensou ordered the heralds to announce his passage as usual when crossing before the gate.

sentences.zh: 翌日請對，具言：“人主非時登樓，則近制咸望恩宥，輦下諸軍亦希賞給。

translations.literal: The next day he requested an audience and fully stated: "When the sovereign ascends a tower at an unscheduled time, those nearby all hope for grace and pardon, and the various armies in the capital also hope for rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he requested an audience and fully stated, "When the sovereign ascends a tower at an unscheduled time, those nearby all hope for grace and pardon, and the various armies in the capital also hope for rewards.

sentences.zh: 臣所以嗬導而過者，欲示眾以陛下非時不登樓也。”

translations.literal: The reason I had them shout the procession and passed by normally was to show the multitude that Your Majesty does not ascend the tower at unscheduled times."
translations.idiomatic: The reason I had them shout the procession and passed by normally was to show the multitude that Your Majesty does not ascend the tower at unscheduled times."

sentences.zh: 太祖善之。

translations.literal: Taizu approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu approved of this.

sentences.zh: 憲府舊例，月賞公用茶，中丞受錢一萬，公用不足則以贓罰物充。

translations.literal: By old custom of the censorate, each month public-use tea was rewarded; the censor-in-chief received ten thousand in cash, and if public funds were insufficient, confiscated goods from corruption cases were used to make up the difference.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom of the censorate, each month public-use tea was rewarded. The censor-in-chief received ten thousand in cash, and if public funds were insufficient, confiscated goods from corruption cases were used to make up the difference.

sentences.zh: 溫叟惡其名不取。

translations.literal: Wensou loathed the name of this and did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Wensou loathed the taint of this practice and did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 任臺丞十二年，屢求代。

translations.literal: He served as censorate commissioner for twelve years and repeatedly requested a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censorate commissioner for twelve years and repeatedly requested a replacement.

sentences.zh: 太祖難其人，不允。

translations.literal: Taizu found no one to replace him and did not grant the request.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu found no one to replace him and did not grant the request.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年被疾，太祖知其貧，就賜器幣，數月卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao he fell ill; Taizu knew he was poor and sent gifts of vessels and silks to his home. Several months later he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao he fell ill. Taizu knew he was poor and sent gifts of vessels and silks to his home. Several months later he died, at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 溫叟事繼母以孝聞，雖盛暑非冠帶不敢見。

translations.literal: Wensou was famed for filial service to his stepmother; even in the height of summer he would not see her unless fully dressed in cap and sash.
translations.idiomatic: Wensou was famed for filial service to his stepmother. Even in the height of summer he would not see her unless fully dressed in cap and sash.

sentences.zh: 五代以來，言執禮者惟溫叟焉。

translations.literal: Since the Five Dynasties, when one spoke of observing ritual, it was Wensou alone.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Five Dynasties, when one spoke of observing ritual, it was Wensou alone.

sentences.zh: 立朝有德望，精賞鑒，門生中尤器楊徽之、趙鄰幾，後皆為名士。

translations.literal: In court he had virtue and prestige, and was skilled in appraisal; among his students he especially valued Yang Huizhi and Zhao Linji, who later both became eminent men.
translations.idiomatic: In court he had virtue and prestige, and was skilled in appraisal. Among his students he especially valued Yang Huizhi and Zhao Linji, who later both became eminent men.

sentences.zh: 范杲幼時，嘗以文贄溫叟，大加稱獎，以女妻之。

translations.literal: When Fan Gao was young he once presented a literary work to Wensou, who greatly praised it and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Gao was young he once presented a literary work to Wensou, who greatly praised it and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 太宗在晉邸，聞其清介，遣吏遺錢五百千，溫叟受之，貯廳西舍中，令府吏封署而去。

translations.literal: When Taizong was at the Prince of Jin's residence, hearing of Wensou's integrity he sent an official to present five hundred thousand in cash. Wensou accepted it, stored it in the western wing of the hall, had the prefectural clerk seal it, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was at the Prince of Jin's residence, hearing of Wensou's integrity he sent an official to present five hundred thousand in cash. Wensou accepted it, stored it in the western wing of the hall, had the prefectural clerk seal it, and departed.

sentences.zh: 明年重午，又送角黍、執扇，所遣吏即送錢者，視西舍封識宛然，還以白太宗。

translations.literal: The next year on the Double Fifth Festival he again sent rice dumplings and a hand fan; the official sent was the same one who had brought the money. Seeing the seal on the western wing intact, he returned and reported this to Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year on the Double Fifth Festival he again sent rice dumplings and a hand fan. The official sent was the same one who had brought the money. Seeing the seal on the western wing intact, he returned and reported this to Taizong.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：“我錢尚不用，況他人乎？

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Even my money he would not use—how much less anyone else's?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Even my money he would not use—how much less anyone else's?

sentences.zh: 昔日納之，是不欲拒我也；

translations.literal: In accepting it then, he did not wish to reject me;
translations.idiomatic: In accepting it then, he did not wish to reject me;

sentences.zh: 今周歲不啟封，其苦節愈見。”

translations.literal: now that a full year has passed without breaking the seal, his austere integrity is all the more evident."
translations.idiomatic: now that a full year has passed without breaking the seal, his austere integrity is all the more evident."

sentences.zh: 命吏輦歸邸。

translations.literal: He ordered the official to have it carted back to the residence.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the official to have it carted back to the residence.

sentences.zh: 是秋，太宗侍宴後苑，因論當世名節士，具道溫叟前事，太祖再三賞歎。

translations.literal: That autumn, while attending a banquet in the rear garden, Taizong discussed eminent men of integrity in the age and fully recounted Wensou's earlier conduct; Taizu repeatedly praised and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, while attending a banquet in the rear garden, Taizong discussed eminent men of integrity in the age and fully recounted Wensou's earlier conduct. Taizu repeatedly praised and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，子炤罷徐州觀察推官待選，以貧詣登聞求注官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, his son Zhao, having left his post as administrative aide to the Xuzhou Observation Commissioner and awaiting selection, went in poverty to the Petition Gate to request registration for office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongxi, his son Zhao, having left his post as administrative aide to the Xuzhou Observation Commissioner and awaiting selection, went in poverty to the Petition Gate to request registration for office.

sentences.zh: 及引對，太宗問誰氏子，炤以溫叟對。

translations.literal: When he was brought in for audience, Taizong asked whose son he was; Zhao answered that he was Wensou's son.
translations.idiomatic: When he was brought in for audience, Taizong asked whose son he was. Zhao answered that he was Wensou's son.

sentences.zh: 太宗愀然，召宰相語其事，且言當今大臣罕有其比。

translations.literal: Taizong looked grave, summoned the chief minister to tell him of the matter, and said that among great ministers today few could compare with Wensou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong looked grave, summoned the chief minister to tell him of the matter, and said that among great ministers today few could compare with Wensou.

sentences.zh: 因問：“炤當得何官？”

translations.literal: He then asked: "What office should Zhao receive?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked, "What office should Zhao receive?"

sentences.zh: 宰相言：“免選以為厚恩。”

translations.literal: The chief minister said: "Exempting him from selection would already be a generous favor."
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister said, "Exempting him from selection would already be a generous favor."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“其父有清操，錄其子登朝，庶足示勸。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "His father had integrity; enrolling his son at court would suffice to show encouragement."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "His father had integrity. Enrolling his son at court would suffice to show encouragement."

sentences.zh: 擢炤太子右讚善大夫，歷判三司理欠、憑由司，江南轉運司，入朝為司封郎中。

translations.literal: Zhao was promoted to Right Supplementation Master of the Heir Apparent, and successively served as director of the Three Offices' Arrears and Voucher Bureaus, the Jiangnan Transport Commission, and upon entering court became Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was promoted to Right Supplementation Master of the Heir Apparent, and successively served as director of the Three Offices' Arrears and Voucher Bureaus and the Jiangnan Transport Commission. Upon entering court he became Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 炳、燁並進士及第。

translations.literal: Bing and Ye both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Bing and Ye both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 子 燁

translations.literal: Son Ye
translations.idiomatic: Son Ye

sentences.zh: 燁，字耀卿，進士及第。

translations.literal: Ye, courtesy name Yaoqing, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, whose courtesy name was Yaoqing, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 積官秘書省著作郎。

translations.literal: By accumulated service he became Academician in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Academician in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 知龍門縣，群盜殺人，燁捕得之，將械送府，恐道亡去，皆斬之。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Longmen County, when bandits committed murder, Ye captured them. About to send them under restraint to the prefecture, fearing they might escape on the road, he beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Longmen County, he captured a band of murderers. Intending to send them under escort to the prefectural seat, he feared they might escape en route—and so had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 眾服其果。

translations.literal: The multitude admired his resoluteness.
translations.idiomatic: The people respected his decisiveness.

sentences.zh: 通判益州，召還，時王曙治蜀，或言其政苛暴。

translations.literal: As vice prefect of Yizhou, he was recalled. At the time Wang Shu governed Shu, and some said his administration was harsh and violent.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as vice prefect of Yizhou he was recalled to court. Wang Shu was then governing Shu, and some said his administration was harsh and brutal.

sentences.zh: 真宗問：“曙治狀與淩策孰愈？”

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong asked: "Compared with Ling Ce, whose governance is the better—Shu's or his?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong asked, "How does Shu's record of governing compare with Ling Ce's—which is better?"

sentences.zh: 燁曰：“策在蜀，歲豐事簡，故得以寬假民。

translations.literal: Ye said: "When Ce was in Shu, the harvests were abundant and affairs were simple, so he was able to show leniency toward the people.
translations.idiomatic: Ye replied, "When Ce was in Shu the harvests were plentiful and affairs were simple, so he could afford to be lenient with the people.

sentences.zh: 比歲小歉，盜賊竊發，非誅殺不能禁。

translations.literal: In recent years there have been slight crop failures, and bandits have arisen in secret; without execution and killing they cannot be suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the harvests have been somewhat poor and banditry has flared up. Without harsh punishment it cannot be checked.

sentences.zh: 然曙所行，亦未嘗出陛下法外。”

translations.literal: Yet what Shu has done has never gone beyond Your Majesty's laws.
translations.idiomatic: Yet nothing Shu has done has ever exceeded the bounds of Your Majesty's law.

sentences.zh: 帝善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved of his answer.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年，始置監官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi, remonstrance officials were first established.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxi 1 remonstrance officials were first established.

sentences.zh: 帝謂宰相曰：“諫官御史，當識朝廷大體。”

translations.literal: The emperor said to the chief minister: "Remonstrance officials and censors ought to understand the great principles of the court."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chief minister, "Remonstrance officials and censors must understand the court's larger interests."

sentences.zh: 於是以燁為右正言。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ye was appointed Right Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was accordingly appointed Right Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 會歲薦饑，河決滑州，大興力役，饑殍相望。

translations.literal: It happened that there was famine that year; the Yellow River broke through at Huazhou; corvée labor was greatly mobilized; starving corpses lined the roads.
translations.idiomatic: That year famine struck, the Yellow River burst its banks at Huazhou, corvée labor was mobilized on a great scale, and the starving lay dead one after another along the roads.

sentences.zh: 燁請策免宰相，以應天變。

translations.literal: Ye requested that the chief minister be removed by imperial decree to respond to Heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: Ye petitioned that the chief minister be dismissed to answer Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 都城東南有泉出，民爭傳可以已疾，詔即其地建祥源觀。

translations.literal: A spring appeared southeast of the capital; the people all spread word that it could cure illness; an edict ordered a Xiangyuan Abbey built on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: A spring burst forth southeast of the capital, and people widely claimed its water could cure disease. An edict ordered a Xiangyuan Abbey built on the site.

sentences.zh: 燁言其詭妄不經，且亢旱，不可興土木以營不急；

translations.literal: Ye said it was deceitful, absurd, and unsound; moreover there was severe drought—it was wrong to undertake construction for non-urgent purposes.
translations.idiomatic: Ye argued that the claim was absurd and unfounded, and that in a time of severe drought it was wrong to launch construction projects for no pressing need.

sentences.zh: 又請罷提點刑獄，禁民棄父母事佛老者。

translations.literal: He also requested abolishing the Intendant of Criminal Affairs, and forbidding the people to abandon their parents to follow Buddhism or Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that regional judicial intendants be abolished and that people be forbidden to forsake their parents for Buddhist or Daoist religious life.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received response.
translations.idiomatic: None of his petitions received a response.

sentences.zh: 表請補外，帝以燁屢言事，乃以判三司戶部勾院，出安撫京西。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting an outside appointment. Because Ye frequently spoke on affairs, the emperor made him director of the Three Offices' Household Bureau Audit Office and sent him out as Pacification Commissioner of West Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking for an outside post. Because Ye had repeatedly remonstrated, the emperor appointed him director of the Three Offices' Household Bureau Audit Office and sent him out as Pacification Commissioner of West Jing.

sentences.zh: 還，直集賢院，同修起居注，遷右司諫。

translations.literal: Upon return he served at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, jointly compiled the Diary of Activity and Repose, and was promoted to Remonstrance Official of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he was assigned to the Hall of Assembled Worthies, helped compile the imperial diary, and was promoted to Remonstrance Official of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 以尚書工部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事，權判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: As Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief handling miscellaneous affairs, he was acting director of the Ministry of Personnel's In-Passing Selection Office.
translations.idiomatic: As Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief in charge of miscellaneous cases, he acted as director of the Ministry of Personnel's in-passing selection office.

sentences.zh: 請京朝官遭父母憂，官司毋得奏留，故事當起復者如舊。

translations.literal: He requested that when capital officials suffered parental mourning, the offices must not memorialize to retain them; established cases where resumption of office was permitted should remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that when capital officials entered mourning for a parent, offices be forbidden to petition to keep them on duty, while established cases permitting resumption of office should remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 因詔益、梓、利、夔路長吏，仍舊奏裁，餘乞免持服者論其罪。

translations.literal: Accordingly an edict ordered that chief officials of the Yi, Zi, Li, and Kui circuits might still memorialize for imperial decision, while others requesting exemption from wearing mourning would be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: chief officials of the Yi, Zi, Li, and Kui circuits might still petition for the throne's decision, but all others who sought to be excused from observing mourning would be punished.

sentences.zh: 改三司戶部副使，擢龍圖閣待制，提舉諸司庫務，權發遣開封府事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Three Offices' Household Bureau, promoted to Attendant-in-Waiting at the Hall of Dragon Illustrations, placed in charge of the various treasury offices, and given interim authority over Kaifeng Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Commissioner of the Three Offices' Household Bureau, promoted to Attendant-in-Waiting at the Hall of Dragon Illustrations, put in charge of the various treasury offices, and given interim authority over Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累遷刑部郎中、龍圖閣直學士、知河南府，徙河中府，卒。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice, Direct Academician at the Hall of Dragon Illustrations, and prefect of Henan; was transferred to Hezhong Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Director in the Ministry of Justice and Direct Academician at the Hall of Dragon Illustrations, served as prefect of Henan, was transferred to Hezhong Prefecture, and died there.

sentences.zh: 初，王曙坐寇準貶官，在朝無敢往見者。

translations.literal: At first, when Wang Shu was demoted on account of Kou Zhun, no one at court dared go to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Shu was demoted on Kou Zhun's account, no one at court dared visit him.

sentences.zh: 燁歎曰：“友朋之義，獨不行於今歟？”

translations.literal: Ye sighed and said: "The duty of friendship—does it alone have no place in the present age?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye sighed and said, "Has the bond of friendship ceased to apply in our own time?"

sentences.zh: 往餞之，經宿而還。

translations.literal: He went to fare him on his way and returned after a night's stay.
translations.idiomatic: He went to see him off and did not return until the next morning.

sentences.zh: 嘗善河中處士李瀆，瀆死，為陳其高行，詔以著作郎贈之。

translations.literal: He had once been close to the reclusive scholar Li Du of Hezhong. When Du died, Ye set forth his lofty conduct, and an edict posthumously awarded him Academician in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been friends with the reclusive scholar Li Du of Hezhong. When Du died, Ye memorialized about his exemplary conduct, and the throne posthumously granted him the title of Academician in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 唐末五代亂，衣冠舊族多離去鄉里，或爵命中絕而世系無所考。

translations.literal: In the chaos of late Tang and the Five Dynasties, many old gentry families left their native places, or their ranks and fates were cut off and their genealogies could no longer be traced.
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos of late Tang and the Five Dynasties, many old gentry families scattered from their homelands; some saw their offices and lines extinguished and their genealogies lost beyond recovery.

sentences.zh: 惟劉氏自十二代祖北齊中書侍郎環俊以下，仕者相繼，而世牒具存焉。

translations.literal: Only the Liu clan, from the twelfth-generation ancestor Huanjun, Vice Director of the Secretariat in Northern Qi, downward, had officeholders in succession, and their clan register remained fully preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Liu clan, from their twelfth-generation ancestor Huanjun—Vice Director of the Secretariat under Northern Qi—downward, produced officeholders in unbroken succession, with their genealogical records fully intact.

sentences.zh: 子几。

translations.literal: His son was Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ji.

sentences.zh: 孫 几

translations.literal: Grandson Ji
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Ji

sentences.zh: 几，字伯壽，以燁任為將作監主簿。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Boshou, through Ye's patronage became Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, whose courtesy name was Boshou, entered office as Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Works through Ye's influence.

sentences.zh: 生而豪俊，長折節讀書，第進士。

translations.literal: By nature bold and heroic, in maturity he restrained himself to study and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and spirited by nature, he later applied himself to study and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 從范仲淹辟，通判邠州。

translations.literal: Following Fan Zhongyan's summons, he became vice prefect of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited by Fan Zhongyan, he was appointed vice prefect of Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 邠地鹵，民病遠汲，几浚渠引水注城中。

translations.literal: Bin's terrain was saline; the people suffered from drawing water from afar. Ji dredged a canal to bring water into the city.
translations.idiomatic: The land around Bin was brackish and the people suffered from having to draw water from far away. Ji dug a canal to channel water into the city.

sentences.zh: 役興，客曰：“自郭汾陽城此州，苟外水可釃，何待今日？

translations.literal: When the work began, a guest said: "Since Guo Ziyi walled this prefecture, if outside water could be used for filtering, why wait until today?
translations.idiomatic: When the project began, a visitor said, "Since Guo Ziyi fortified this prefecture, if outside water could have been brought in, why wait until now?

sentences.zh: 無為虛費勞人也！”

translations.literal: Do not waste labor in vain!
translations.idiomatic: Do not waste everyone's labor in vain!

sentences.zh: 几不答。

translations.literal: Ji did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Ji made no reply.

sentences.zh: 未幾，水果至，鑿五池於通逵，民大便利。

translations.literal: Before long, water indeed arrived; he cut five pools at the thoroughfare, greatly benefiting the people.
translations.idiomatic: Before long water did arrive. He excavated five pools along the main thoroughfare, to the people's great benefit.

sentences.zh: 孫沔薦其才堪將帥，換如京使、知寧州。

translations.literal: Sun Mian recommended that his talent suited command; he was transferred to Palace Envoy and made prefect of Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mian recommended him as capable of military command. He was transferred to Palace Envoy and appointed prefect of Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俗喜巫，軍校仗妖法結其徒，亂有日。

translations.literal: The local custom favored shamanism; a military officer relied on sorcery to gather followers, and rebellion was imminent.
translations.idiomatic: The people there were fond of shamanism. A military officer used occult arts to gather a following, and an uprising seemed only days away.

sentences.zh: 几使他兵伏壘門以伺，夜半盡禽之。

translations.literal: Ji sent other troops to lie in ambush at the camp gate and wait; at midnight he captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Ji posted other troops in ambush at the camp gate. At midnight they captured the entire band.

sentences.zh: 加本路兵馬鈐轄、知邠州。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Coordinator of the circuit's military forces and prefect of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Coordinator of the circuit's military forces and prefect of Bin.

sentences.zh: 儂智高犯嶺南，几上書願自效，以為廣東、西捉殺。

translations.literal: When Nong Zhigao invaded Lingnan, Ji submitted a memorial offering himself, and was made Suppression Commissioner of Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Nong Zhigao invaded the Lingnan region, Ji volunteered his services and was appointed Suppression Commissioner for Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 道聞蔣偕、張忠戰沒，疾馳至長沙，見狄青曰：“賊若退守巢穴，瘴毒方興，當班師以俟再舉。

translations.literal: On the road he heard that Jiang Xie and Zhang Zhong had died in battle; he galloped to Changsha and said to Di Qing: "If the rebels withdraw to their lair and miasma is rising, we should withdraw the army and wait for another campaign.
translations.idiomatic: En route he learned that Jiang Xie and Zhang Zhong had fallen in battle. He galloped to Changsha and told Di Qing, "If the rebels fall back to their strongholds while the miasma season is coming on, we should withdraw and wait for another offensive.

sentences.zh: 若恃勝求戰，此成擒耳。”

translations.literal: If they rely on victory and seek battle, this will mean their capture.
translations.idiomatic: If they grow overconfident and come out to fight, they will be easy prey."

sentences.zh: 賊果悉眾來，大戰於歸仁鋪。

translations.literal: The rebels indeed came out with their full force; a great battle was fought at Guirenpu.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did indeed march out in full force, and a great battle was fought at Guirenpu.

sentences.zh: 前鋒孫節死，几以右軍搏鬥，自辰至巳，勝負未決。

translations.literal: The vanguard commander Sun Jie died; Ji fought with the right wing from the chen hour to the si hour, victory undecided.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard commander Sun Jie was killed. Ji fought with the right wing from morning until mid-morning, but the outcome remained in doubt.

sentences.zh: 几言於青，出勁騎五千，張左右翼搗其中堅，賊駭潰。

translations.literal: Ji said to Qing: send out five thousand elite cavalry, deploy left and right wings to strike their center, and the rebels were terrified and routed.
translations.idiomatic: Ji urged Qing to commit five thousand elite cavalry, send them against the enemy center from both flanks, and the rebels broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 進皇城使、知涇州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Imperial Inner City and made prefect of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Imperial Inner City and appointed prefect of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陛見，辭以母老，丐復文階歸養。

translations.literal: At audience he declined on grounds of an aged mother, requesting restoration to civil rank to return home in support.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he declined the post on the grounds that his mother was elderly, asking to be restored to civil rank so he could return home to care for her.

sentences.zh: 仁宗諭之曰：“涇，內地也，將母莫便焉。”

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong instructed him: "Jing is interior territory—nowhere better to bring one's mother."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong told him, "Jing lies in the interior. There is no better place to keep your mother nearby."

sentences.zh: 命特賜冠帔。

translations.literal: He ordered special bestowal of cap and robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered special gifts of cap and ceremonial robes for his mother.

sentences.zh: 領循州刺史，遷西上閣門使，再歸郎中班。

translations.literal: He held the title of prefect of Xunzhou, was promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner, and again returned to the director rank sequence.
translations.idiomatic: He held the nominal post of prefect of Xunzhou, was promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner, and then returned once more to the civil director rank.

sentences.zh: 曾公亮薦之，復以嘉州團練使為太原、涇原路總管。

translations.literal: Zeng Gongliang recommended him; he was again made regimental commissioner of Jiazhou and overall commander of the Taiyuan and Jingyuan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On Zeng Gongliang's recommendation he was again appointed regimental commissioner of Jiazhou and overall commander of the Taiyuan and Jingyuan circuits.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇周家堡，轉運使陳述古攝渭帥，几移文索援兵，不聽，率諸將偕請，又不聽，乃趣以手書。

translations.literal: When the Tangut people raided Zhoujiabao, Transport Commissioner Chen Shugu was acting Wei commander. Ji sent an official communication requesting reinforcements but was refused; leading the generals together he petitioned again and was again refused; then he pressed the matter with a personal letter.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tanguts attacked Zhoujiabao, Transport Commissioner Chen Shugu was acting commander of Wei. Ji formally requested reinforcements but was refused. He then led the generals in a joint petition and was refused again, and finally pressed the matter with a personal letter.

sentences.zh: 述古怒，移几為鳳翔，且劾生事。

translations.literal: Shugu was angry, transferred Ji to Fengxiang, and also impeached him for causing trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Shugu grew angry, had Ji transferred to Fengxiang, and impeached him for stirring up trouble.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以總管非轉運使所得徙置，遣御史出按，述古黜，几亦改鄜州。

translations.literal: The court held that the overall commander was not within the transport commissioner's authority to transfer and dismiss; it sent out a censor to investigate. Shugu was dismissed, and Ji was also transferred to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court ruled that a transport commissioner had no authority to move an overall commander and dispatched a censor to investigate. Shugu was dismissed, and Ji was reassigned to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召判三班院。

translations.literal: He was summoned to direct the Three Ranks Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as director of the Three Ranks Bureau.

sentences.zh: 邊吏告夏人趨大順，英宗問几。

translations.literal: Border officials reported that the Tanguts were heading for Dashun; Emperor Yingzong asked Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials reported that the Tanguts were moving on Dashun. Emperor Yingzong consulted Ji.

sentences.zh: 几曰：“大順天險，非夏人可得近，正恐與趙明為仇爾。”

translations.literal: Ji said: "Dashun has Heaven's natural defenses; the Tanguts cannot approach it—this likely stems from enmity with Zhao Ming, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Dashun is a natural fortress the Tanguts cannot easily reach. I suspect this is really a feud with Zhao Ming, nothing more."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“明之子奔馬入城，幾為所掩，卿料敵一何神也。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ming's son galloped his horse into the city and was nearly overrun—how divinely you read the enemy!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Ming's son barely escaped on horseback when they rushed the city—you read the enemy uncannily well."

sentences.zh: 以為秦鳳總管。

translations.literal: He was made overall commander of Qin and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed overall commander of Qin and Feng.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，轉四方館使、知保州，治狀為河北第一。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Ji was transferred to Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall and prefect of Bao Prefecture; his governance record ranked first in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong ascended the throne, Ji became Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall and prefect of Bao Prefecture. His record of governance ranked first in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 逾六年，即請老，還為秘書監致仕。

translations.literal: After more than six years he immediately requested retirement and returned as Retired Overseer of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After six years he asked to retire and was granted the post of Retired Overseer of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，祀明堂，大臣言几知音，詔詣太常定雅樂。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng, at the Bright Hall sacrifice, great ministers said Ji understood musical pitch; an edict ordered him to go to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to fix the ceremonial music.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfeng, during the Bright Hall sacrifice, leading ministers said Ji understood musical pitch. An edict summoned him to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to set the ceremonial music.

sentences.zh: 几曰：“古樂備四清聲，沿五季亂離廢，請增之。”

translations.literal: Ji said: "Ancient music had all four clear tones; along the Five Dynasties through chaos and dispersal they were abandoned—I request they be restored."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Ancient music employed all four clear tones, but they were abandoned amid the chaos of the Five Dynasties. I ask that they be restored."

sentences.zh: 樂成，予一子官。

translations.literal: When the music was completed, one of his sons was granted office.
translations.idiomatic: When the music was completed, one of his sons was granted an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 几得謝二十年，放曠嵩、少間，遇唐末異人靖長宮者得養生訣，故益老不衰。

translations.literal: Ji had been retired twenty years, roaming freely between Song and Shao peaks; he met the late-Tang eccentric Jing Changgong and obtained the secret of nurturing life, and so grew ever older without decline.
translations.idiomatic: Ji spent twenty years in retirement, wandering freely among Mount Song and the lesser peaks. He met the late-Tang recluse Jing Changgong and learned the secrets of longevity, and so only grew more vigorous with age.

sentences.zh: 間與人語邊事，謂張耒曰：“比見詔書禁邊吏夜飲。

translations.literal: Occasionally speaking with others on border affairs, he said to Zhang Lei: "Recently I saw an edict forbidding border officials to drink at night.
translations.idiomatic: Once, discussing border affairs with others, he said to Zhang Lei, "I recently saw an edict forbidding frontier officers to drink at night.

sentences.zh: 此曹一旦有急，將使輸其肝腦，此平日禁其為樂，為今役者不亦難乎？

translations.literal: When these men have sudden emergency, you will want them to offer their lives—yet on ordinary days you forbid their pleasure; will those you now employ not find it difficult?
translations.idiomatic: When crisis comes you expect these men to lay down their lives. Yet in peacetime you forbid them even simple pleasure—how can you expect ready service when trouble strikes?"

sentences.zh: 夫椎牛釃酒，豐犒而休養之，非欲以醉飽為德，所以增士氣也。”

translations.literal: Butchering cattle and straining wine, richly rewarding them and letting them rest—is not to treat drunkenness and fullness as virtue, but to raise morale.
translations.idiomatic: Feasting them with butchered cattle and strained wine, giving them generous rewards and time to rest—that is not indulgence for its own sake, but the way to raise their fighting spirit."

sentences.zh: 耒敬識其語。

translations.literal: Lei respectfully noted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Lei respectfully committed his words to memory.

sentences.zh: 再加通議大夫，卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Grandee of Counselling and died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grandee of Counselling and died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 几篤於風義，推父遺恩官從兄，已得任子，必先兄弟子之孤者。

translations.literal: Ji was deeply devoted to honor and righteousness; when extending his father's lingering favor to appoint a cousin, though he already had a hereditary appointment for his own son, he always gave priority to orphaned sons of his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was deeply devoted to honor and righteousness. When using his father's remaining patronage to secure office for a cousin, though his own son already held a hereditary appointment, he always gave priority to orphaned nephews.

sentences.zh: 其議樂律最善，以為：“律主於人聲，不以尺度求合。

translations.literal: His discussions of musical pitch and law were best; he held: "Pitch laws take human voice as their basis; one should not seek accord through measuring rods alone.
translations.idiomatic: He was at his best discussing pitch and tuning, holding that "pitch standards should follow the human voice, not be forced to conform to measure alone."

sentences.zh: 古今異時，聲亦隨變，猶以古冠服加於今人，安得而稱。

translations.literal: Past and present differ in time, and sound likewise changes—just as putting ancient cap and robe on a man of today, how could it fit?
translations.idiomatic: Times change, and so does the quality of sound. Imposing ancient cap and robes on a man of today—how could they be made to fit?"

sentences.zh: 儒者泥古，致詳於形名度數間，而不知清濁輕重之用，故求於器雖合，而考於聲則不諧。”

translations.literal: Confucian scholars cling to antiquity, pursuing detail in names, forms, and measures, yet not knowing the use of clarity and turbidity, lightness and weight; thus seeking accord in instruments though matching, when tested in sound they are not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars cling to antiquity, fussing over names, forms, and numbers while missing what clarity, turbidity, lightness, and weight actually do. Their instruments may match on paper, yet when tested by ear the tones fail to harmonize."

sentences.zh: 嘗遊佛寺，聞鍾聲，曰：“聲澌而悲，主者且不利。”

translations.literal: Once visiting a Buddhist temple, hearing the bell, he said: "The sound is faint and mournful—the abbot will soon meet misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: Once at a Buddhist temple he heard the bell and said, "That tone is thinning and mournful—the abbot will soon come to harm."

sentences.zh: 是夕，主僧死。

translations.literal: That evening the chief monk died.
translations.idiomatic: That very night the chief monk died.

sentences.zh: 在保州，聞角聲，曰：“宮微而商離，至秋，守臣憂之。”

translations.literal: At Bao Prefecture, hearing horn signals, he said: "The gong note is faint and the shang note is displaced—by autumn the guarding official will be troubled."
translations.idiomatic: While at Bao Prefecture he heard the horn signals and said, "The gong is faint and the shang misplaced—by autumn the local commander will be in trouble."

sentences.zh: 及期，几遇疾。

translations.literal: When the time came, Ji fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: When autumn came, Ji himself fell ill.

sentences.zh: 然所學頗雜鄭、衛云。

translations.literal: Yet what he studied was rather mixed with Zheng and Wei music, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: It was said, however, that his learning also leaned rather heavily toward licentious Zheng and Wei music.

sentences.zh: 劉濤，字德潤，徐州彭城人，後唐天成中，舉進士，釋褐為鳳翔掌書記，拜右拾遺，賜緋。

translations.literal: Liu Tao, courtesy name Derun, was a native of Pengcheng in Xuzhou. In the middle of Tiancheng under Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination, took his first office as secretary at Fengxiang, was appointed Right Reminder, and was granted crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tao, whose courtesy name was Derun, came from Pengcheng in Xuzhou. In the Tiancheng era of Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination, entered office as secretary at Fengxiang, was appointed Right Reminder, and was granted crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 時太常丞史在德上章，詞理鄙俗，仍犯廟諱。

translations.literal: At the time Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Shi Zaide submitted a memorial whose wording was vulgar in argument and also violated taboo names of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Shi Zaide, submitted a memorial whose language was crude and also violated ancestral temple name taboos.

sentences.zh: 濤上言請正其罪，雖不允，時論是之。

translations.literal: Tao submitted a memorial requesting that his crime be corrected; though not granted, contemporary opinion approved.
translations.idiomatic: Tao memorialized asking that he be punished. Though the request was denied, public opinion sided with Tao.

sentences.zh: 出為山南東道節度判官，召為左補闕，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: He went out as judicial aide to the military governor of Shannan East Circuit, was recalled as Left Supplementation Master, and was promoted to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: He served as aide to the military governor of Shannan East Circuit, was recalled as Left Supplementation Master, and was promoted to Diarist.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，改司勳員外郎、史館修撰，遷工部郎中，賜金紫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu under Jin he was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel's Merits Bureau and Compiler of the Historiography Institute, promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works, and granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianfu era under Later Jin he became Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel's Merits Bureau and Compiler of the Historiography Institute, rose to Director in the Ministry of Works, and was granted gold and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 歷度支、職方二郎中，掌左藏庫。

translations.literal: He successively served as Director in the Revenue and Credentials bureaus, and managed the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Director in the Revenue and Credentials bureaus and managed the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 時少帝奢侈，常以銀易金，廣其器皿。

translations.literal: At the time the young emperor was extravagant, often exchanging silver for gold to enlarge his vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor was extravagant at the time, often trading silver for gold to enlarge his ceremonial vessels.

sentences.zh: 李崧判三司，令上庫金之數。

translations.literal: Li Song directed the Three Offices and ordered the count of gold in the upper treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song, director of the Three Offices, ordered a tally of the gold in the upper treasury.

sentences.zh: 及崧以元簿較之，少數千鎰。

translations.literal: When Song compared it with the original ledger, it was short by several thousand ingots.
translations.idiomatic: When Song checked the figure against the original ledger, the count fell short by several thousand ingots.

sentences.zh: 崧責曰：“帑庫通式，一日不受虛數，毫厘則有重典。”

translations.literal: Song rebuked him: "The treasury regulations—for a single day they accept no false numbers; even a hair's breadth brings severe punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Song rebuked him, saying, "Treasury regulations allow no false count for even a single day. The slightest discrepancy carries severe punishment."

sentences.zh: 濤曰：“帑司常有報不盡數，以備宣索。”

translations.literal: Tao said: "The treasury office often reports less than the full count, to reserve for imperial requisitions."
translations.idiomatic: Tao replied, "The treasury office habitually reports less than the full amount, keeping a reserve against sudden imperial requisitions."

sentences.zh: 崧令有司劾濤，濤事迫，以情告樞密使桑維翰，乃止罰一月奉。

translations.literal: Song ordered the relevant office to impeach Tao. Tao, pressed by the affair, confided the circumstances to Chief Councilor Sang Weihan, and the punishment was limited to one month's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Song had the authorities impeach Tao. Hard pressed, Tao confided the truth to Chief Councilor Sang Weihan, and the penalty was reduced to one month's salary.

sentences.zh: 漢初，宰相蘇禹珪薦為中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, Chief Minister Su Yugui recommended him as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Later Han, Chief Minister Su Yugui recommended him for the post of Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，坐令子監察御史頊代草誥命，左遷少府少監，分司西京；

translations.literal: In Guangshun of Zhou, for the offense of having his son, Supervising Censor Xu, draft edicts in his place, he was demoted to Vice Director of the Palace Supplies Office and assigned to the Western Capital as a supernumerary official;
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangshun era of Later Zhou, Tao was demoted to Vice Director of the Palace Supplies Office and assigned to the Western Capital as a supernumerary official on the charge that he had his son, Supervising Censor Xu, draft edicts for him.

sentences.zh: 頊亦貶復州司戶。

translations.literal: Xu was also demoted to Revenue Clerk of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was also demoted to Revenue Clerk of Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，就改太常少卿，俄拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, he was immediately changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; soon he was appointed Right Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiande era, he was promptly transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and soon appointed Right Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee.

sentences.zh: 四年，再知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he again directed the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again directed the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 樞密使王樸嘗薦童子劉譜於濤，濤不納，樸銜之。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Wang Pu once recommended the youth Liu Pu to Tao; Tao did not accept him, and Pu harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Wang Pu once recommended the prodigy Liu Pu to Tao, but Tao would not take him, and Pu thereafter bore him a grudge.

sentences.zh: 時世宗南征在迎鑾，濤引新及第人赴行在。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Shizong was on campaign in the south at Yingluan; Tao brought newly passed jinshi to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Shizong was campaigning in the south at Yingluan, Tao brought the newly passed jinshi to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 樸時留守上都，飛章言濤取士不精。

translations.literal: Pu was then stationed at the capital and sent urgent memorials saying Tao's selection of scholars was not rigorous.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was then left in charge at the capital and sent urgent memorials accusing Tao of selecting scholars without sufficient rigor.

sentences.zh: 世宗命翰林學士李昉覆試，出者七人。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Hanlin Academician Li Fang to re-examine them; seven were eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Hanlin Academician Li Fang to re-examine the candidates, and seven were failed.

sentences.zh: 濤坐責授太子右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: Tao was punished and appointed Right Supporter of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was punished and appointed Right Supporter of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，遷右詹事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gongdi ascended, he was transferred to Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gongdi ascended the throne, he was transferred to Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 濤性剛毅不撓，素與宰相范質不協，常鬱鬱不得志，遂退居洛陽之清化里，杜門以書史自娛。

translations.literal: Tao's nature was firm and unyielding; he had long been at odds with Chief Minister Fan Zhi, was often depressed and frustrated, and so retired to Qinghua Lane in Luoyang, closing his doors and taking pleasure in books and history.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was by nature resolute and unyielding. He had long been at odds with Chief Minister Fan Zhi, lived in constant frustration, and finally withdrew to Qinghua Lane in Luoyang, shutting his doors and finding solace in books and history.

sentences.zh: 太祖素知濤履行，開寶二年召赴闕，以老病求退，授秘書監致仕。

translations.literal: The Taizu had long known Tao's conduct; in the second year of Kaibao he was summoned to court, but pleaded old age and illness to retire and was granted Superintendent of the Secretariat with retirement honors.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu had long known Tao's character. In Kaibao 2 he was summoned to court, but pleaded old age and illness and was granted Superintendent of the Secretariat with retirement honors.

sentences.zh: 年七十二卒。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，中書舍人盧導受詔主文，將鎖宿，濤力薦薛居正，以為文章器業必至臺輔，導取之，後果為相。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, Secretariat Drafter Lu Dao received an edict to preside over the examinations and was about to lock himself in for the seclusion period; Tao strongly recommended Xue Juzheng, holding that his literary talent and capacity would surely reach the highest offices; Dao selected him, and he later indeed became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingtai era, Secretariat Drafter Lu Dao received an edict to preside over the examinations and was about to begin the seclusion period. Tao strongly recommended Xue Juzheng, declaring that his literary talent and capacity would surely carry him to the highest offices. Dao selected him, and he later indeed became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 世稱其知人。

translations.literal: The age praised him for knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries praised him for knowing men well.

sentences.zh: 頊子晟，晟子訥、譚，並進士及第。

translations.literal: Xu's son Sheng; Sheng's sons Ne and Tan—all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's son Sheng, and Sheng's sons Ne and Tan, all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 晟至屯田員外郎，訥為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Sheng rose to Vice Director in the Agriculture Bureau; Ne became Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng rose to Vice Director in the Agriculture Bureau, and Ne became Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 邊光範

translations.literal: Bian Guangfan
translations.idiomatic: Bian Guangfan

sentences.zh: 邊光範，字子儀，幷州陽曲人。

translations.literal: Bian Guangfan, courtesy name Ziyi, was a native of Yangqu in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Guangfan, whose courtesy name was Ziyi, came from Yangqu in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性謙退和雅，有吏材。

translations.literal: His nature was modest, retiring, and refined; he had talent for administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was modest, unassuming, and refined by nature, and had a gift for administration.

sentences.zh: 父仁嗣，忠武軍節度副使。

translations.literal: His father Rensi was deputy military governor of the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rensi served as deputy military governor of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 光範，後唐天成二年，起家榆次令，召為殿中丞，賜緋。

translations.literal: Guangfan, in the second year of Tiancheng under Later Tang, began his career as magistrate of Yuci, was summoned as Director in the Palace Administration, and was granted crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: Guangfan began his career in Tiancheng 2 of Later Tang as magistrate of Yuci, was summoned as Director in the Palace Administration, and was granted crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 長興四年，改太常丞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing, he was changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing 4 he was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱。

translations.literal: He mourned the death of his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，服闋，授檢校戶部員外郎、北京留守判官兼侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu under Jin, when mourning ended, he was appointed Titular Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, judicial aide to the regent of the Northern Capital, and concurrently Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianfu era under Later Jin, when his mourning ended, he was appointed Titular Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, judicial aide to the regent of the Northern Capital, and concurrently Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜太府少卿。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Treasury.

sentences.zh: 上書曰：“臣聞唐太宗有言：‘朕居深宮之中，視聽不能及遠，所委者惟都督、刺史。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that Emperor Taizong of Tang said: 'I dwell deep within the palace; sight and hearing cannot reach far. Those to whom I entrust affairs are only regional commanders and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant has heard that Emperor Taizong of Tang said, 'I dwell deep within the palace, and what I see and hear cannot reach far. Those to whom I entrust affairs are only regional commanders and prefects.

sentences.zh: ’則知此官實係治亂，必須得人。

translations.literal: ' From this one knows these offices truly bear on order and disorder; men of ability must be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: ' From this one knows that these offices truly bear on order and disorder, and that men of ability must be chosen.

sentences.zh: 今則刺史或因緣世祿，或貢奉家財，或微立軍功，或但循官序。

translations.literal: Today prefects may advance through hereditary emolument, or by presenting family wealth as tribute, or by slight military merit, or merely by following the sequence of office.
translations.idiomatic: Today prefects may rise through hereditary emolument, by presenting family wealth as tribute, by slight military merit, or merely by following the ordinary sequence of promotion.

sentences.zh: 實恐撫民無術，御吏無方，以此牧民，而民受其賜鮮矣。

translations.literal: I truly fear they have no method to comfort the people, no way to control officials; governing the people thus, the people receive little benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I truly fear that they have no skill in comforting the people and no method for controlling officials. Governing the people in this way, the people receive little benefit indeed.

sentences.zh: 望選能吏以蘇民瘼，用致升平。”

translations.literal: I hope able administrators may be chosen to relieve the people's distress and thereby bring about peace and order."
translations.idiomatic: I hope that able administrators may be chosen to relieve the people's distress and thereby bring about peace and order."

sentences.zh: 奏入，留中不出。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but kept within the palace and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but kept within the palace and not issued.

sentences.zh: 俄為冊秦王李從嚴副使。

translations.literal: Soon he served as deputy envoy in conferring the title of Prince on Li Congyan, King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served as deputy envoy in the investiture of Li Congyan as Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 張從恩以外戚為河南尹，奏授判官。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong'en, as an imperial in-law, became Governor of Henan and memorialized to appoint him judicial aide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong'en, an imperial in-law, became Governor of Henan and memorialized to appoint Guangfan as his judicial aide.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書監兼御史中丞，入拜大理少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Superintendent of the Secretariat and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, entered court as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Superintendent of the Secretariat and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, then entered court as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 漢初，改檢校刑部尚書、衛尉卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, he was changed to Titular Minister of Justice and Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Later Han he was transferred to Titular Minister of Justice and Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 上言：“伏見朝廷除刺史，不限年月，或未及期年，又聞除代。

translations.literal: He submitted: "Your servant observes that when the court appoints prefects, no fixed term of years is set; sometimes before a full year has passed, word comes of replacement.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant observes that when the court appoints prefects, no fixed term of years is set. Sometimes before a full year has passed, word already comes of replacement.

sentences.zh: 往來跋涉，豈暇撫懷。

translations.literal: Coming and going in long journeys—how can they find leisure to comfort and cherish?
translations.idiomatic: Traveling back and forth on long journeys, how can they find leisure to comfort and care for the people?

sentences.zh: 望慎選良牧，立定年限，以責輯綏之效。”

translations.literal: I hope good governors may be carefully chosen and fixed terms established, to hold them accountable for the effect of their pacification and governance."
translations.idiomatic: I hope that good governors may be carefully chosen and fixed terms established, so that they may be held accountable for the results of their pacification and governance."

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but no response was given.

sentences.zh: 乾祐二年，連使宋州虞城、汝州襄城，按視民田之傷稼者。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyou, he was consecutively sent to Yucheng in Song Prefecture and Xiangcheng in Ru Prefecture to inspect civilian fields damaged by crops.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyou 2 he was sent in succession to Yucheng in Song Prefecture and Xiangcheng in Ru Prefecture to inspect civilian fields damaged by crop failure.

sentences.zh: 是冬，為吳越加恩使。

translations.literal: That winter he served as envoy to extend imperial favor to Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he served as envoy to extend imperial favor to Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，出知陳州，遷秘書監，俄召拜御史中丞，賜襲衣、銀器、繒彩、鞍勒馬，復為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun of Zhou, he went out as prefect of Chen Prefecture, was promoted to Superintendent of the Secretariat, soon recalled and appointed Censor-in-Chief, granted court robes, silver vessels, silk brocade, and saddled horses, and again made Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangshun era of Later Zhou he was sent out as prefect of Chen Prefecture, promoted to Superintendent of the Secretariat, and soon recalled and appointed Censor-in-Chief. He was granted court robes, silver vessels, silk brocade, and saddled horses, and again made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時禮部侍郎於貢部或掌或否，光範拜官，將及秋試，乃言於執政曰：“單門偶進，何言名第。

translations.literal: At the time the Vice Minister of Rites sometimes did or did not oversee the examination bureau; Guangfan received his appointment as the autumn examinations drew near, and said to the chief ministers: "From a humble household by chance advanced—what talk of rank and degree.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Vice Minister of Rites sometimes did and sometimes did not oversee the examination bureau. Guangfan received his appointment as the autumn examinations drew near, and said to the chief ministers, "From a humble household I was advanced by chance—what talk is there of rank and degree?

sentences.zh: 若他曹公事，光範不敢辭；

translations.literal: If it is the public business of another bureau, Guangfan would not dare decline;
translations.idiomatic: If it is the public business of another bureau, Guangfan would not dare decline it;

sentences.zh: 若處文衡，校閱名賢，品藻優劣，非下走所能。”

translations.literal: but if it is presiding over the literary scales, reviewing famous worthies, and judging merit and flaw—that is beyond what this lowly servant can do."
translations.idiomatic: but if it is presiding over the literary scales, reviewing famous worthies, and judging merit and flaw—that is beyond what this lowly servant can do."

sentences.zh: 執政曰：“公晉末為翰林、樞密直學士，勿避事也。”

translations.literal: The chief ministers said: "You were a Hanlin Academician and Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat at the end of Jin—do not shirk the duty."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers said, "You were a Hanlin Academician and Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat at the end of Later Jin. Do not shirk the duty."

sentences.zh: 及期，光節辭疾不出，乃以翰林學士承旨徐台符掌之，時論多其自知。

translations.literal: When the time came, Guangfan pleaded illness and did not appear; Hanlin Academician-in-Charge Xu Taifu was then placed in charge, and contemporary opinion largely approved his self-knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came, Guangfan pleaded illness and did not appear. Hanlin Academician-in-Charge Xu Taifu was then placed in charge, and contemporary opinion largely approved his self-knowledge.

sentences.zh: 宋初，征澤、潞，命光範為前軍轉運，計度鄭、洛、汝、孟、懷芻糧。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, when campaigning against Ze and Lu, he was ordered to serve as transport commissioner for the advance army, calculating and supplying fodder and grain for Zheng, Luo, Ru, Meng, and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song, when campaigning against Ze and Lu, he was ordered to serve as transport commissioner for the advance army, calculating and supplying fodder and grain for Zheng, Luo, Ru, Meng, and Huai.

sentences.zh: 秋，拜太常卿。

translations.literal: In autumn he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時張昭為吏部尚書，朝議以其耆老，令光範簽判選事。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Zhao was Minister of the Civil Service; court discussion held that because of his great age, Guangfan was ordered to countersign and judge selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Zhao was Minister of the Civil Service. Court discussion held that because of his great age, Guangfan was ordered to countersign and judge selection affairs.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，襄州節度慕容延釗征湖南，以光範權知州事，路當衝會，餉饋無闕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong, when Military Governor Murong Yanzhao of Xiang Prefecture campaigned in Hunan, Guangfan was appointed acting prefect; the route was a critical junction, and provisions were never lacking.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 4, when Military Governor Murong Yanzhao of Xiang Prefecture campaigned in Hunan, Guangfan was appointed acting prefect. The route was a critical junction, and provisions were never lacking.

sentences.zh: 是冬郊祀，召還。

translations.literal: That winter, at the suburban sacrifice, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, at the suburban sacrifice, he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 會延釗卒，復知襄州。

translations.literal: When Yanzhao died, he again served as prefect of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhao died, he again served as prefect of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 大軍數萬由陝路討蜀，出漢上，光範復當供億，人不知勞。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of troops marched by the Shaan route to chastise Shu, emerging on the Han; Guangfan again bore responsibility for supplies, and the people felt no burden.
translations.idiomatic: When tens of thousands of troops marched by the Shaan route to chastise Shu and emerged on the Han, Guangfan again bore responsibility for supplies, and the people felt no burden.

sentences.zh: 嘗舉本鎮判官李楫為殿中侍御史，楫後坐事除籍，光範左遷太子賓客，仍知襄州。

translations.literal: He once recommended his circuit's judicial aide Li Ji as Imperial Censor; Ji was later struck from the rolls for an offense, and Guangfan was demoted to Retainer of the Heir Apparent while still serving as prefect of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He once recommended his circuit's judicial aide Li Ji as Imperial Censor. Ji was later struck from the rolls for an offense, and Guangfan was demoted to Retainer of the Heir Apparent while still serving as prefect of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 五年，兼橋道使，朝廷遣使督治道，常六七輩，一使所調發民皆數百人，吏緣為奸，多私取民課，所發不充數，而道益不修。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he concurrently served as Commissioner for Bridge and Road Works; the court sent envoys to supervise road repair, often six or seven at a time; each envoy's requisition mobilized several hundred civilians; clerks used this as cover for fraud, privately taking the people's labor levies; what was requisitioned fell short, and the roads grew worse instead of better.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he concurrently served as Commissioner for Bridge and Road Works. The court sent envoys to supervise road repair, often six or seven at a time. Each envoy's requisition mobilized several hundred civilians. Clerks used this as cover for fraud and privately took the people's labor levies. What was requisitioned fell short, and the roads grew worse instead of better.

sentences.zh: 光範計其工，以州卒代民，官給器用，役不淹久，人以無擾。

translations.literal: Guangfan calculated the labor needed, used district soldiers in place of civilians, supplied tools from the government, and kept service from dragging on; people found it undisturbing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangfan calculated the labor required, used district soldiers in place of civilians, supplied tools from the government, and kept service from dragging on. The people found the work undisturbing.

sentences.zh: 詔書褒美。

translations.literal: An edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his work.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，復判吏部銓曹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao, he again served as acting head of the Ministry's selection bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 4 he again served as acting head of the Ministry's selection bureau.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞劉溫叟卒，以光範判御史臺事，數月，真拜中丞。

translations.literal: When Censor-in-Chief Liu Wensou died, Guangfan was placed in charge of the Censorate; after several months he was formally appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor-in-Chief Liu Wensou died, Guangfan was placed in charge of the Censorate. After several months he was formally appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 六年，以疾解銓曹任。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on account of illness he relinquished his post in the selection bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, on account of illness, he relinquished his post in the selection bureau.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 光範性至孝，謙退和易，雅有吏幹。

translations.literal: Guangfan's nature was deeply filial; he was modest, retiring, and easy in manner, and had elegant talent for administration.
translations.idiomatic: Guangfan was deeply filial by nature, modest and easy in manner, and had an elegant gift for administration.

sentences.zh: 母病疽，光範嘗吮之。

translations.literal: When his mother suffered from an abscess, Guangfan once sucked it.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother suffered from an abscess, Guangfan once sucked the wound.

sentences.zh: 景德中，錄其孫易從同學究出身。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era, his grandson Yicong was enrolled for office on the basis of the same scholar status.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingde era his grandson Yicong was granted office on the basis of the same scholar status.

sentences.zh: 劉載，字德輿，涿州范陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Zai, courtesy name Deyu, was a native of Fanyang in Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zai, whose courtesy name was Deyu, came from Fanyang in Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐盧龍節度濟之六世孫。

translations.literal: Sixth-generation descendant of Ji, military governor of Lulong under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He was a sixth-generation descendant of Ji, military governor of Lulong under Tang.

sentences.zh: 父昭，下蔡令。

translations.literal: His father Zhao was magistrate of Xia Cai.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao served as magistrate of Xia Cai.

sentences.zh: 載，後唐清泰中舉進士。

translations.literal: Zai, in Qingtai of Later Tang, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zai passed the jinshi examination during the Qingtai era of Later Tang.

sentences.zh: 晉初，解褐校書郎，遷著作佐郎，賜緋，拜左拾遺、集賢殿直學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, he took his first office as collator, was promoted to Assistant Compiler, granted crimson robes, and appointed Left Reminder and Academician-in-Attendance of the Hall for Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Later Jin he entered office as collator, was promoted to Assistant Compiler, granted crimson robes, and appointed Left Reminder and Academician-in-Attendance of the Hall for Worthies.

sentences.zh: 漢初，為殿中侍卿御史，丁內艱，服闋，復拜舊官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, he served as Attendant Censor-in-Chief; he mourned his mother, and when mourning ended was again appointed to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Later Han he served as Imperial Censor. After entering mourning for his mother and completing the mourning period, he was again appointed to his former office.

sentences.zh: 判西京留臺，改倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served as judicial officer of the Western Capital regency and was changed to Vice Director in the Granaries Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial officer of the Western Capital regency and was transferred to Vice Director in the Granaries Bureau.

sentences.zh: 嘗著五論，曰《為君》、《為相》、《為將》、《去讒》、《納諫》，頗為文士所稱。

translations.literal: He once composed five treatises titled "On Being Ruler," "On Being Chief Minister," "On Being General," "On Removing Slander," and "On Accepting Remonstrance," which literary men much praised.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed five treatises titled "On Being Ruler," "On Being Chief Minister," "On Being General," "On Removing Slander," and "On Accepting Remonstrance," which literary men much praised.

sentences.zh: 周世宗初，擢知制誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong of Zhou, he was elevated to Drafting Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the reign of Shizong of Later Zhou, he was elevated to Drafting Edicts.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年，拜右諫議大夫，與右拾遺鄭起、尚書博士李寧同校道書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande, he was appointed Right Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee, and together with Right Reminder Zheng Qi and Doctor of the Masters Bureau Li Ning collated Daoist texts.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiande 3 he was appointed Right Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee and, together with Right Reminder Zheng Qi and Doctor of the Masters Bureau Li Ning, collated Daoist texts.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，使許州定田租。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and sent to Xu Prefecture to fix land tax.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and sent to Xu Prefecture to fix land tax assessments.

sentences.zh: 俄賜金紫，為魏王符彥卿加恩國信使。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted gold and purple and served as imperial envoy to extend favor to Fu Yanqing, Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was granted gold and purple robes and served as imperial envoy to extend favor to Fu Yanqing, Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 宋初，浚五丈河，自陳橋達曹州之西境，命護其役。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, when dredging the Wuzhang River from Chen Bridge to the western border of Cao Prefecture, he was ordered to oversee the labor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song, when the Wuzhang River was dredged from Chen Bridge to the western border of Cao Prefecture, he was ordered to oversee the labor.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，貝州節度使張光翰來朝，遣載權知州事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong, when Military Governor Zhang Guanghan of Bei Prefecture came to court, Zai was dispatched to serve as acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 4, when Military Governor Zhang Guanghan of Bei Prefecture came to court, Zai was dispatched to serve as acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 光翰歸鎮，載還，知貢舉。

translations.literal: When Guanghan returned to his command, Zai came back and directed the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanghan returned to his command, Zai came back and directed the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，掌建安榷貨務。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande, he managed the Jian'an Monopoly Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qiande era he managed the Jian'an Monopoly Bureau.

sentences.zh: 六年，就為江南國主生辰使，召還，令知鎮州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he immediately served as birthday envoy to the lord of Jiangnan; recalled, he was ordered to govern Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as birthday envoy to the lord of Jiangnan. Recalled, he was ordered to govern Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，坐與何繼筠不協，改山南東道行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao, for failing to get along with He Jiyun, he was changed to Adjutant of the campaign staff of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 4, for failing to get along with He Jiyun, he was transferred to Adjutant of the campaign staff of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十年不召，嘗受詔權點檢州事。

translations.literal: For ten years he was not summoned; he once received an edict to serve temporarily as inspector of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years he was not summoned to court. He once received an edict to serve temporarily as inspector of prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，復入為給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he again entered service as Palace Attendant.
