translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taiping Xingguo era he again entered service as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 三年，出知襄州，六年，代還。

translations.literal: In the third year he went out as prefect of Xiang; in the sixth year he was replaced and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he went out as prefect of Xiang; in the sixth year he was replaced and returned.

sentences.zh: 告老，改工部侍郎致仕，乃賜一子出身。

translations.literal: He requested retirement; was changed to Vice Minister of Works with retirement honors, and one son was granted office by imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement and was granted the post of Vice Minister of Works with retirement honors. One son was then granted office by imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died at age seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 載尤好學，博通史傳，善屬文。

translations.literal: Zai was especially fond of learning, thoroughly versed in historical texts, and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was especially fond of learning, thoroughly versed in historical texts, and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 嘗受詔撰明憲皇后諡冊文，又作《吊戰國賦》萬餘言行於世。

translations.literal: He once received an edict to compose the posthumous title document for Empress Mingxian, and also wrote "Elegy on the Warring States," more than ten thousand characters in circulation in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He once received an edict to compose the posthumous title document for Empress Mingxian, and also wrote "Elegy on the Warring States," more than ten thousand characters in length, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 雅信釋典，敦尚名節。

translations.literal: He deeply trusted Buddhist scripture and earnestly upheld reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply trusted Buddhist scripture and earnestly upheld reputation and integrity.

sentences.zh: 子宗言，至比部郎中。

translations.literal: His son Zongyan rose to Director in the Finance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongyan rose to Director in the Finance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 宗望，景德二年進士及第。

translations.literal: Zongwang passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang passed the jinshi examination in Jingde 2.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年，其孫介以載文集來獻，以為試將作主簿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, his grandson Jie presented Zai's collected writings and was made provisional chief clerk on trial.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 4 his grandson Jie presented Zai's collected writings and was made provisional chief clerk on trial.

sentences.zh: 程羽，字冲遠，深州陸澤人。

translations.literal: Cheng Yu, courtesy name Chongyuan, was a native of Luze in Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu, whose courtesy name was Chongyuan, came from Luze in Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少好學，能屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and could compose texts.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved learning and could compose texts.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，擢進士第，授陽穀主簿。

translations.literal: In Tianfu of Jin he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Yanggu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era of Later Jin he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Yanggu.

sentences.zh: 歷虞鄉、醴泉、新都令，皆有政績。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Yuxiang, Liquan, and Xindu, and in each had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Yuxiang, Liquan, and Xindu, and in each post had notable administrative achievements.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，選為兩使判官，入對，太祖詢以時事，敷奏稱旨，擢著作郎，出知興州。

translations.literal: In Kaibao he was selected as judicial aide to a diplomatic envoy; entering audience, the Taizu inquired about current affairs; his full presentation pleased the emperor, and he was promoted to Compiler and sent out as prefect of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era he was selected as judicial aide to a diplomatic envoy. Entering audience, the Taizu inquired about current affairs. His full presentation pleased the emperor, and he was promoted to Compiler and sent out as prefect of Xing.

sentences.zh: 逾年，改知興元府。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to administer Xingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made administrator of Xingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔歸闕，以本官領開封府判官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict recalled him to court; he retained his original office and concurrently served as judicial investigator of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was recalled to court and, while keeping his rank, was made judicial investigator of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 羽性淳厚，蒞事恪謹。

translations.literal: Yu was by nature sincere and generous, and in conducting affairs he was scrupulously careful.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was sincere and generous by nature and conducted every duty with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 時太宗尹京，頗以長者待之。

translations.literal: At that time the future Taizong was administering the capital and treated him rather as an elder.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the future Taizong governed the capital and treated him with the respect due an elder.

sentences.zh: 及即位，拜給事中，知開封府。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, Yu was appointed Attendant Gentleman and made administrator of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Yu was appointed Attendant Gentleman and administrator of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出知成都府，為政寬簡，蜀人便之。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as administrator of Chengdu; his government was lenient and simple, and the people of Shu found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as administrator of Chengdu. His rule was lenient and unburdensome, and the people of Shu were well served.

sentences.zh: 入朝，拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: On entering court he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court he was made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 上欲優以清職。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to honor him with a pure office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to honor him with a prestigious court post.

sentences.zh: 故事，端明殿設學士二員，居翰林學士上，專備顧問，馮道、趙鳳始居是職，累朝因之。

translations.literal: By precedent the Duanming Hall had two academicians, ranking above Hanlin academicians and devoted solely to consultation. Feng Dao and Zhao Feng first held these posts, and successive dynasties followed the practice.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the Duanming Hall had two academicians who ranked above the Hanlin and served solely as imperial advisers. Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were the first to hold the post, and successive dynasties kept the custom.

sentences.zh: 及是，即殿名以羽為文明殿學士，位在樞密副使下，且即泰寧坊營第以賜之。

translations.literal: On this occasion, taking the hall's name, Yu was made Academician of the Hall of Civilization, ranking below the Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, and a residence was built for him in Taining Ward and bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion Yu was made Academician of the Hall of Civilization, ranking below the Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, and a mansion was built for him in Taining Ward as a gift.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，典試貢士，御試得人居多。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he directed the examination of tribute scholars; in the imperial examination many of those he selected proved capable.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 5 he directed the civil examinations, and many of those who passed the palace test under his charge proved outstanding.

sentences.zh: 六年，以老疾求解職，拜兵部侍郎，未幾致仕，仍給全奉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on account of age and illness he requested to leave office; he was appointed Vice Minister of War, and before long retired, while still receiving his full salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he asked to retire because of age and illness. He was made Vice Minister of War and soon retired, while still receiving his full salary.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 1 he died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子希振，以蔭至尚書虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Xizhen, by yin privilege, reached Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works in the Department of Parks.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xizhen, through yin privilege, rose to Outer Gentleman in the Ministry of Works' Department of Parks.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Dazhong Xiangfu 1.

sentences.zh: 其子適，賜同學究出身。

translations.literal: His son Shi was granted the status of a fellow licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi was granted the status of a fellow licentiate.

sentences.zh: 從孫琳，別傳。

translations.literal: His collateral descendant Lin has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His collateral descendant Lin is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：五季為國，不四、三傳輒易姓，其臣子視事君猶傭者焉，主易則他役，習以為常。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the Five Dynasties as states, within three or four generations the surname would change. Their ministers and subjects regarded serving a lord like hired laborers: when the master changed they took another task, and this became habitual.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: During the Five Dynasties, thrones changed every few reigns. Ministers treated service to a ruler like hired labor—when the master changed they simply took a new employer, until this became normal.

sentences.zh: 故唐方滅即北面於晉，漢甫稱禪已相率下拜於周矣。

translations.literal: Thus when Tang had just perished they at once faced north to Jin; when Han had barely proclaimed the abdication they already bowed in succession to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang had barely fallen when they turned to Jin; Han had scarcely abdicated when they were already bowing to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 君子傷之，此《雜臣傳》所繇立也。

translations.literal: Men of principle grieved at this; that is why the 'Biographies of Miscellaneous Ministers' was established.
translations.idiomatic: Men of principle were grieved by this—hence the 'Biographies of Miscellaneous Ministers.'

sentences.zh: 李穀、邊歸讜、竇貞固、李濤輩，或在廟堂，或侍帷幄，世主之所寵任，社稷之所倚賴，而更事異姓，不能以名節生死，倫義廢矣。

translations.literal: Li Gu, Bian Guidang, Dou Zhengu, Li Tao, and their kind—some in the ancestral temple hall, some attending within the curtain—were favorites of successive rulers and pillars on whom the altars of state relied, yet they served other surnames and could not stake their fame and integrity on life or death. Human duty was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu, Bian Guidang, Dou Zhengu, Li Tao, and men like them—whether in the council hall or at the emperor's side—were trusted by successive rulers and relied upon by the state, yet they served new dynasties and would not stake their honor on life or death. Moral obligation was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 且穀以籌策自名，乃不能料藝祖有容人之量，及受李筠饋遺，懼其見殺，遂以憂死，又何繆耶？

translations.literal: Moreover Gu made his name by strategy, yet could not foresee that Taizu had the magnanimity to tolerate men, and after accepting Li Jun's gifts feared he would be put to death and so died of grief—how absurd!
translations.idiomatic: Gu moreover made his name as a strategist, yet failed to see that Taizu was magnanimous enough to spare him. After accepting Li Jun's gifts he feared execution and died of anxiety—how mistaken!

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，魏范粲、齊顏見遠，宜見褒於前史也。

translations.literal: Alas! Fan Can of Wei and Yan Jingyouan of Qi saw far ahead; they ought to be praised in the earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—Fan Can of Wei and Yan Jingyouan of Qi saw further than their age; earlier histories were right to honor them.
